title: Optics-microwave Entanglement And State Teleportation Mediated By A Cavity Magnomechanical System
authors: F. Engelhardt, A. V. Bondarenko, A. Metelmann, Ya. M. Blanter, S. Viola Kusminskiy, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating usable output-entanglement in continuous variable systems can serve as a viable resource for improving applications in quantum information science. In this work, we show how to generate steady-state output-entanglement in a two-stage conversion setup between optical and microwave photon which employs resonantly coupled magnetic and mechanical excitations, as proposed in Phys. Rev. Applied 18, 044059 (2022). We show that the entanglement can be maximized for the same set of parameters which optimize the frequency-conversion efficiency, and that it can be leveraged for a teleportation-based state-transfer protocol for coherent input-states with fidelity close to unity. We propose an implementation based on an Yittrium Iron Garnet disk of micrometer scale, and use both simulation results and reasonable estimates to assess the performance under optimized conditions. We find a maximum teleportation fidelity of 0.75 for the proposed setup.
tldr: This paper demonstrates steady-state entanglement generation between optical and microwave photons via a cavity magnomechanical system, achieving high teleportation fidelity for coherent states.
motivation: To generate usable continuous-variable entanglement between optical and microwave domains, which is a key resource for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors propose a two-stage conversion setup using a YIG disk with resonantly coupled magnons and phonons, analyze the steady-state output entanglement, and simulate a teleportation-based state transfer protocol.
result: Entanglement is maximized under parameters that optimize frequency conversion efficiency, and teleportation fidelity up to 0.75 is achieved for coherent input states.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway for generating optical-microwave entanglement in hybrid systems, with potential applications in quantum transducers and quantum communication.

title: Device-Independent Quantum Secret Sharing Protocol Enhanced By Advantage Distillation
authors: Yong-Hui Yang, Jian-Hong Shi, Hong-Wei Li, Hai-Long Zhang, Yun-Teng Yang, Yu-Bing Zhu, Yan-Yang Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Device-independent quantum secret sharing (DI-QSS) provides high security by eliminating the need to trust devices, yet its practical performance is limited by channel loss and noise. This work extends advantage distillation from two-party quantum key distribution (QKD) to three-party DI-QSS, redesigning the corresponding data interaction and verification procedures. The technique is systematically applied to the basic protocol and three active improvement strategies: noise preprocessing, post-selection, and their combination. This approach enhances noise tolerance, reduces the required global detection efficiency threshold, and significantly extends the maximum secure communication distance. Numerical simulations demonstrate that for the basic protocol over fiber, the maximum secure distance increases from 0.16 km to 1.85 km, and the noise tolerance improves from 10.17% to 28.49%. The results show that generalizing advantage distillation to the three-party setting effectively strengthens the protocol's robustness and practicality, enhancing its adaptability to realistic noise and advancing the development of more reliable quantum secret sharing systems.
tldr: This paper extends advantage distillation from two-party QKD to three-party device-independent quantum secret sharing, significantly improving noise tolerance and secure distance.
motivation: Device-independent quantum secret sharing (DI-QSS) suffers from practical limitations due to channel loss and noise, hindering its real-world deployment. The authors aim to enhance its robustness and practicality by adapting advantage distillation techniques from QKD.
method: The authors redesign data interaction and verification procedures to apply advantage distillation to three-party DI-QSS. They systematically integrate it into the basic protocol and three active improvement strategies: noise preprocessing, post-selection, and their combination.
result: Numerical simulations show that for the basic protocol over fiber, the maximum secure distance increases from 0.16 km to 1.85 km, and noise tolerance improves from 10.17% to 28.49%.
conclusion: Generalizing advantage distillation to the three-party setting effectively strengthens DI-QSS protocols, enhancing their adaptability to realistic noise and advancing the development of more reliable quantum secret sharing systems.

title: Phase-tunable Remote Nonreciprocal Charging In Waveguide Qed
authors: Meixi Guo, Jian Huang, Rui-Yang Gong, Xian-Li Yin, Guofeng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Remote quantum batteries require directional and controllable energy transfer between spatially separated quantum nodes, yet most existing protocols rely on direct charger-battery Hamiltonian couplings. Here we propose a phase-tunable waveguide-QED architecture for remote quantum-battery charging, in which a driven charger and a remote battery are coupled solely via engineered waveguide-mediated interference, without any direct local interaction. We systematically compare four configurations: two-giant-emitter and giant-small-emitter hybrids, each with open or mirror-terminated waveguides. By engineering the propagation and coupling phases, the waveguide-mediated coherent exchange interaction and collective dissipation can be balanced to suppress the backward channel while retaining a finite forward channel, thereby realizing cascaded-like unidirectional charging. Our analysis shows that nonreciprocity and storage efficiency can be independently engineered, offering design flexibility for different quantum network scenarios. The giant-small-emitter mirror-terminated configuration simultaneously achieves perfect nonreciprocity and battery-dominated storage, while both giant-small-emitter configurations exhibit distance-insensitive directionality. Extending the scheme to quadratic driving, we show that anomalous second moments render the battery state non-passive, making ergotropy a performance metric distinct from stored energy. These results establish phase-tunable waveguide networks as a versatile platform for remote quantum-energy transfer and provide design principles for directional and work-extractable energy storage in quantum networks.
tldr: A phase-tunable waveguide-QED architecture enables remote, nonreciprocal quantum battery charging without direct coupling, achieving unidirectional energy transfer and independent control of nonreciprocity and storage efficiency.
motivation: Remote quantum batteries require directional energy transfer between spatially separated nodes, but existing protocols rely on direct interactions. This work aims to achieve controllable, unidirectional charging using waveguide-mediated interference.
method: The authors propose a waveguide-QED setup with a driven charger and remote battery coupled via engineered phases, comparing four configurations: two-giant-emitter and giant-small-emitter hybrids with open or mirror-terminated waveguides. They analyze coherent exchange and collective dissipation to realize cascaded-like unidirectional charging.
result: Nonreciprocity and storage efficiency can be independently engineered; the giant-small-emitter mirror-terminated configuration achieves perfect nonreciprocity and battery-dominated storage, while both giant-small-emitter configurations show distance-insensitive directionality. Quadratic driving yields non-passive battery states, making ergotropy a distinct performance metric.
conclusion: Phase-tunable waveguide networks provide a versatile platform for remote quantum energy transfer, offering design principles for directional and work-extractable energy storage in quantum networks.

title: Optimal Quantum Feshbach Engines
authors: Aaron Wandhammer, Vincent Hardel, Paul-Antoine Hervieux, Giovanni Manfredi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an optimization framework for high-efficiency quantum cycles implemented with a trapped Bose-Einstein condensate, whose control parameters are the trap stiffness and the interaction strength tuned via a Feshbach resonance. Optimal driving protocols for each stroke of the cycle are obtained from a variational description of the condensate dynamics combined with Nelson's stochastic quantization, which maps the quantum evolution onto an effective Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. The optimal protocol is obtained by minimizing a user-defined cost functional that selects the best trade-off between protocol duration and arbitrary physical constraints (such as the expended work or the proximity to an adiabatic evolution), and exhibits remarkable stability over repeated cycles. The method also provides a systematic route to optimal control for generic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations, paving the way to optimal control strategies in fields as diverse as nonlinear optics, quantum fluids, and quantum plasmas.
tldr: This paper develops an optimization framework for quantum cycles in a Bose-Einstein condensate, using Feshbach resonance and trap stiffness as control parameters, and applies Nelson's stochastic quantization to derive optimal driving protocols that balance efficiency and duration.
motivation: To achieve high-efficiency quantum heat engines by optimizing control protocols for a trapped BEC, addressing the trade-off between cycle duration and work output or adiabaticity.
method: A variational description of the condensate dynamics combined with Nelson's stochastic quantization maps the quantum evolution onto an effective Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, allowing minimization of a user-defined cost functional that includes protocol duration and physical constraints.
result: Optimal protocols for each stroke of the quantum cycle are obtained, showing remarkable stability over repeated cycles and providing a systematic route to optimal control for nonlinear Schrödinger equations.
conclusion: The method paves the way for optimal control strategies in nonlinear optics, quantum fluids, and quantum plasmas, and can be applied to other quantum thermodynamic cycles.

title: Quantum Purity Amplification For Arbitrary Eigenstates And Multiple Outputs
authors: Zhaoyi Li, Elias Theil, Aram W. Harrow, Isaac Chuang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum purity amplification (QPA) is the task of coherently transforming [MATH] copies of a mixed state into high-fidelity copies of a chosen eigenstate. We solve QPA in the general setting of [MATH] input copies, [MATH] output copies, arbitrary target eigenstates, arbitrary local dimension [MATH], and generic input spectra. We characterize the optimal channel and derive its all-site and one-site performance laws across output regimes. For the asymptotic analysis, we use a path-graph parametrization to show that, when the target eigenvalue has a constant spectral gap [MATH], achieving all-site error [MATH] requires a number of input copies independent of [MATH] and scaling as [MATH]. When [MATH] approaches a constant, the performance exhibits phase-like regimes, which we characterize explicitly. For the nonasymptotic analysis, we develop a theory of generalized Young diagrams that yields tight sample complexity bounds and provides the first dimension-uniform guarantee for optimal QPA. We also provide asymptotically efficient implementations of the optimal protocol. Together, these results establish QPA as a rigorous example of coherent quantum information processing with dimension-uniform sample complexity, supplying the technical foundation for the coherent-incoherent separation developed in the companion work.
tldr: This paper solves quantum purity amplification for arbitrary eigenstates and multiple outputs, providing optimal protocols and sample complexity bounds with dimension-uniform guarantees.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits and optimal protocols for coherently transforming mixed states into high-fidelity eigenstates, which is a primitive for quantum information processing and may have implications for energy consumption of quantum operations.
method: The authors use a path-graph parametrization for asymptotic analysis and develop a theory of generalized Young diagrams for nonasymptotic analysis, deriving optimal channels and performance laws.
result: They characterize the optimal channel and its performance across output regimes, showing that achieving all-site error requires input copies scaling as O(1/δ^2) independent of local dimension, and identify phase-like regimes when the spectral gap approaches a constant.
conclusion: The results establish quantum purity amplification as a rigorous example of coherent quantum information processing with dimension-uniform sample complexity, providing a technical foundation for the coherent-incoherent separation.

title: Testing Superpositions Of Detector Trajectories
authors: Cisco Gooding, Taylor Cey, Robert Mann
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a realizable experiment to test the response of a particle detector prepared in a superposition of locations interacting with a relativistic quantum field. Using a beamsplitter to prepare two superposed branches of a modulated laser probe, these branches are directed to intersect a pancake-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate at two separate locations. The branches are then recombined with another beamsplitter. Heterodyning one of the outputs, the response function corresponding to an Unruh-deWitt detector in a superposition of locations interacting with a (2+1)-dimensional massless scalar field is shown to appear in the difference photocurrent power spectrum. Operating beyond the standard quantum limit using squeezed light, we estimate the signal-to-noise ratio [MATH] for extracting the response function over a broad set of baseband frequencies.
tldr: Proposes an experiment to test the response of a particle detector in a superposition of locations interacting with a quantum field, using a Bose-Einstein condensate and squeezed light.
motivation: To probe the interplay between quantum superposition and relativistic quantum field theory, specifically the Unruh-deWitt detector model, which is foundational for understanding nonlocality and energy constraints.
method: A modulated laser probe is split into two branches via a beamsplitter, directed to intersect a pancake-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate at two locations, then recombined. Heterodyne detection and squeezed light are used to extract the response function from the difference photocurrent power spectrum.
result: The response function for a detector in a superposition of locations interacting with a (2+1)-dimensional massless scalar field appears in the power spectrum, with signal-to-noise ratio estimated using squeezed light beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: The experiment is realizable with current technology and could test fundamental aspects of quantum field theory and detector models, with implications for quantum foundations and possibly quantum communication.

title: A Journey Through Flatland: What Does The Antiflatness Of A Spectrum Teach Us?
authors: Barbara Jasser, Daniele Iannotti, Alioscia Hamma
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the concept of antiflatness to characterize the structural fluctuations within the entanglement spectrum of a quantum state (i.e., the spectrum of its reduced density operator). As a measure of the interplay between entanglement and magic, two fundamental quantum resources, antiflatness provides second-order information about quantum correlations that standard average measures fail to capture. Recognizing that standard majorization theory fundamentally orders states by purity and is structurally blind to spectral fluctuations, we introduce a novel partial ordering known as antiflat majorization, based on the R\'enyi entropy spread. We define Flatness-Preserving Operations (FPOs), establishing new necessary conditions for state convertibility. Furthermore, we unify different measures of antiflatness-such as Capacity of Entanglement, Linear R\'enyi spread, and Logarithmic antiflatness-using the frameworks of escort distributions and Bregman divergences. We prove that the Capacity of Entanglement can be expressed as a second derivative of the Kullback-Leibler divergence along the escort trajectory, connecting it with the Quantum Fisher Information. Finally, we demonstrate that absolute maximal antiflatness is not achieved by a single universal state, but rather by a continuous Pareto frontier of extremal states with jump spectra, and we analyze the typicality of these spectral fluctuations using Haar, Bures-Hall and t-doped Clifford random state ensembles.
tldr: Introduces antiflatness as a measure of spectral fluctuations in entanglement spectra, linking entanglement and magic, and proposes a new majorization theory based on Rényi entropy spread.
motivation: Standard entanglement measures ignore spectral fluctuations; the authors aim to capture second-order correlations and unify measures of antiflatness.
method: Defines antiflat majorization and Flatness-Preserving Operations (FPOs); uses escort distributions and Bregman divergences to unify capacity of entanglement, linear Rényi spread, and logarithmic antiflatness; analyzes typicality via random state ensembles.
result: Capacity of entanglement equals second derivative of KL divergence along escort trajectory, connecting to quantum Fisher information; absolute maximal antiflatness is achieved by a Pareto frontier of states with jump spectra, not a single state.
conclusion: Antiflatness provides a refined characterization of quantum correlations, with implications for state convertibility and resource theories; future work may explore experimental signatures and applications in quantum information.

title: Athena: A Compiler For Optimized Scheduling In Distributed Quantum Computers
authors: Won Joon Yun (the University Of Texas At Austin), Dhilan Nag (the University Of Texas At Austin), Sneha Ballabh (the University Of Texas At Austin), Jiapeng Zhao (cisco Quantum Lab), Eneet Kaur (cisco Quantum Lab), Poulami Das
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed Quantum Computers (DQCs) enable large system sizes by connecting smaller chips via photonic interconnects. DQCs use teleportation to relocate qubits and execute CNOTs between qubits on different chips. However, non-local CNOTs are 4.3-7.7[MATH] slower and 4[MATH] more error-prone than local CNOTs within a chip, which degrades program fidelities. Existing compilers group CNOTs with overlapping qubits into blocks and collectively optimize teleportations for each block. However, block-level scheduling has two key drawbacks. First, it lacks lookahead ability across blocks because it selects the optimal schedule for one block before proceeding to the next. As a result, it cannot assess the impact of a teleportation on future blocks. Our studies show that naively expanding the lookahead window to include subsequent blocks does not address this issue. Second, existing approaches do not schedule future block operations or the teleportations they require until preceding blocks are fully scheduled, introducing delay and latency overheads. We propose ATHENA, a DQC compiler that addresses these limitations using two key insights: Utility-driven Lookahead with Multi-Candidate Block Scheduling (UMS) and EPR-Capacity-Aware Early Scheduling (EES). UMS schedules a block by considering only useful future blocks in its lookahead window. A future block has utility if it shares overlapping qubits with the current block being scheduled. UMS also maintains multiple schedules during compilation, allowing it to defer commitment to globally sub-optimal schedules early in the compilation process. EES enables ATHENA to schedule future operations and their relocations early when EPR resources are available. Our evaluations show that ATHENA reduces teleportations by 34% on average and up to 65%, and reduces latency by 2[MATH] on average and up to 2.9[MATH] compared to the state-of-the-art.
tldr: ATHENA is a compiler for distributed quantum computers that reduces teleportations and latency by using utility-driven lookahead and early EPR scheduling.
motivation: Existing DQC compilers suffer from lack of lookahead across blocks and delayed scheduling, leading to suboptimal teleportation and latency overheads.
method: ATHENA introduces Utility-driven Lookahead with Multi-Candidate Block Scheduling (UMS) to consider only useful future blocks, and EPR-Capacity-Aware Early Scheduling (EES) to schedule future operations early when EPR resources are available.
result: ATHENA reduces teleportations by 34% on average (up to 65%) and reduces latency by 2x on average (up to 2.9x) compared to state-of-the-art.
conclusion: The work demonstrates significant improvements in distributed quantum computing compilation, with implications for quantum network efficiency and scalability.

title: Concatenating Algebraic Codes Over High-Rate Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Adam Wills, Michael E. Beverland, Lev S. Bishop, Jay M. Gambetta, Patrick Rall, Vikesh Siddhu, Andrew W. Cross
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Different quantum error correction schemes trade off overhead, error suppression, and hardware connectivity. Code concatenation can relax these tradeoffs by using an outer code whose non-local connectivity is supplied by logical operations of an inner code rather than directly by hardware. Prior works showed that this can reduce memory overhead for local low-rate inner codes such as the surface code. Here, we study concatenation over non-local, high-rate inner codes. Such inner codes experience correlated errors among the many logical qubits in a single codeblock. We handle this by treating each block as a single logical Galois qudit, enabling concatenation with algebraic outer codes with excellent parameters and, crucially, list decoders. In particular, we consider a memory system formed by concatenating quantum Reed-Solomon outer codes over the gross code. For fault-tolerant syndrome extraction, we develop a Galois qudit Shor scheme using "time-like" Reed-Solomon protection against measurement errors. Interestingly, a lightweight fault tolerance scheme, that would fail for qubits, works well for large-alphabet qudits, suggesting a very different theory of fault tolerance for such qudits. The whole protocol is optimised via improved bicycle instruction logical error rates, novel compilation strategies, and recent decoder post-selection rules. At uniform [MATH] physical noise, the concatenated gross code reaches the teraquop regime, which it previously could not access, with a lower space overhead than the [MATH]-qubit two-gross code, while offering several advantages from the engineering standpoint. Beyond our main case study, we believe the core ideas of Galois qudits, quantum Reed-Solomon outer codes, and list decoding, will prove generically powerful and highly transferable ideas across high-rate quantum architectures.
tldr: This paper proposes concatenating algebraic outer codes with high-rate quantum LDPC inner codes to improve memory overhead and error suppression, using Galois qudits and list decoding.
motivation: To overcome tradeoffs between overhead, error suppression, and connectivity in quantum error correction, especially for high-rate inner codes that suffer from correlated logical errors.
method: Treat each block of a high-rate inner code as a single Galois qudit, concatenate with quantum Reed-Solomon outer codes, and develop a fault-tolerant syndrome extraction scheme using time-like Reed-Solomon protection.
result: The concatenated gross code reaches the teraquop regime with lower space overhead than the two-gross code, and lightweight fault tolerance works well for large-alphabet qudits.
conclusion: Galois qudits, quantum Reed-Solomon outer codes, and list decoding are powerful tools for high-rate quantum architectures, with potential applications beyond this case study.

title: Thermodynamic Irreversibility Of Training Algorithms
authors: Liu Ziyin, Yuanjie Ren, Adam Levine, Isaac Chuang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The training algorithms for AI systems all introduce far-from-equilibrium dynamical processes, and understanding the irreversibility of these algorithms is a fundamental step towards understanding the learning dynamics of modern AI systems. In this work, we establish a general framework for defining and analyzing the irreversibility of training algorithms. We show that four different ways to characterize the irreversibility of dynamical processes are equivalent to leading order in the step size [MATH]: numerical backward error [MATH], time-renormalized correction [MATH], microscopic time reversal asymmetry [MATH], and the (regularized) stochastic-thermodynamic entropy production [MATH]. The irreversibility gives rise to a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking emergent force that generically breaks non-isometric continuous reparametrization symmetries, preserves orthogonal symmetries, and leads to a universal preference for those learning trajectories that minimize the entropy production rate.
tldr: This paper establishes a general framework linking irreversibility of training algorithms to stochastic-thermodynamic entropy production, showing equivalence of four irreversibility measures and revealing symmetry-breaking forces that favor minimal entropy production trajectories.
motivation: Training algorithms for AI systems involve far-from-equilibrium dynamics; understanding their irreversibility is fundamental to learning dynamics.
method: The authors define and analyze irreversibility via numerical backward error, time-renormalized correction, microscopic time reversal asymmetry, and regularized stochastic-thermodynamic entropy production, proving their equivalence to leading order in step size.
result: Irreversibility gives rise to a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking emergent force that breaks non-isometric continuous reparametrization symmetries, preserves orthogonal symmetries, and leads to a universal preference for trajectories minimizing entropy production rate.
conclusion: The framework provides a thermodynamic perspective on training algorithms, with implications for understanding learning dynamics and designing more efficient algorithms.

title: Photon Blockade Via Three-body Interactions: Toward High-purity And Bright Single-photon Sources
authors: Peng-Bo Li Sheng Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photon blockade is vital for single-photon generation, but current schemes with conventional and unconventional photon blockade face critical limitations like the purity-brightness trade-off, hindering the generation of high-performance single-photons. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a fundamentally new photon blockade mechanism by utilizing three-body interactions between a single photonic mode and two qubits. This kind of interaction intrinsically cuts off the excitation path to the two-photon state, resulting in a perfect photon blockade effect. The mechanism operates across a broad parameter range, free from the constraints of strong coupling or weak driving. Remarkably, it breaks the purity-brightness trade-off, enabling the simultaneous achievement of extreme purity and high brightness, both significantly outperforming previous mechanisms. Furthermore, this approach demonstrates robustness against thermal noise and avoids unwanted oscillations in the time-delayed correlation function. This work provides a path for generating high-purity, high-brightness, and robust single-photon sources, a key resource for quantum technologies.
tldr: This paper proposes a new photon blockade mechanism using three-body interactions between a photonic mode and two qubits to achieve high-purity and high-brightness single-photon sources, overcoming the purity-brightness trade-off.
motivation: Current photon blockade schemes suffer from a trade-off between purity and brightness, limiting the performance of single-photon sources. The authors aim to overcome this limitation by introducing a fundamentally new mechanism.
method: The authors introduce three-body interactions between a single photonic mode and two qubits, which intrinsically cuts off the excitation path to the two-photon state, resulting in perfect photon blockade. They analyze the system's performance across a broad parameter range without requiring strong coupling or weak driving.
result: The mechanism achieves extreme purity and high brightness simultaneously, significantly outperforming previous mechanisms. It also demonstrates robustness against thermal noise and avoids unwanted oscillations in the time-delayed correlation function.
conclusion: This work provides a path for generating high-purity, high-brightness, and robust single-photon sources, which are key resources for quantum technologies. The approach may inspire further studies on three-body interactions in quantum optics.

title: Geometric Construction Of Optimal Teleportation Witnesses
authors: Yanning Jia, Fenzhuo Guo, Mengxuan Bai, Mengyan Li, Haifeng Dong, Fei Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Not all entangled states are useful for quantum teleportation. We present a geometric method to construct optimal teleportation witnesses, which provide operational necessary and sufficient criteria for identifying the teleportation usefulness of arbitrary two-qudit entangled states. Specifically, by developing a two-layer iterative cutting-plane algorithm to solve the shortest distance problem from the target state [MATH] to the convex set [MATH] of useless states, we obtain the projection point [MATH] and then construct the optimal teleportation witness from the projection geometry. Moreover, the shortest distance [MATH] obtained during this construction also serves as a necessary and sufficient criterion for usefulness. We apply our method to identify the teleportation usefulness of three classes of entangled states.
tldr: A geometric method using a two-layer iterative cutting-plane algorithm constructs optimal teleportation witnesses to identify which entangled states are useful for quantum teleportation.
motivation: Not all entangled states are useful for teleportation; existing criteria are often not necessary and sufficient. The authors aim to provide an operational, geometric criterion.
method: They develop a two-layer iterative cutting-plane algorithm to solve the shortest distance problem from a target state to the convex set of useless states, obtaining a projection point and constructing the optimal teleportation witness from the projection geometry.
result: The shortest distance serves as a necessary and sufficient criterion for teleportation usefulness. The method is applied to three classes of entangled states, demonstrating its effectiveness.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for identifying useful entangled states for teleportation, with potential applications in quantum network design and entanglement distillation.

title: dSABRE: A SABRE-Style Router For Multi-Core Distributed Quantum Computers
authors: Sanjiang Li
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimising EPR consumption is the dominant objective when routing a quantum circuit on a distributed quantum computer (DQC). We present dSABRE, a SABRE-style router for multi-core processors that, on each iteration of a lookahead-driven loop, first resolves any intra-core front-layer gates by SWAP scoring and only falls back to scoring inter-core teleportation candidates when the intra-core front is empty. Three mechanisms drive the improvement over the state of the art: a five-term gate-centric teleportation score that generalises the local SWAP heuristic to the inter-core setting, whose explicit capacity-penalty term keeps the scorer from teleporting into saturated cores; a proactive congestion-relief pass that redistributes idle qubits out of high-demand cores before deadlock; and a BFS-layer construction of the inter-core extended set that respects DAG dependencies layer by layer rather than mixing wires in topological order. Across 18 MQT-Bench circuits at 25, 36, and 64 logical qubits, dSABRE reduces geometric-mean EPR consumption by 41-44% over TeleSABRE and by 16-68% over the gate-teleportation-based pytket-dqc, using standard Qiskit SabreLayout for the initial layout. A large-circuit QFT sweep at 100-360 qubits confirms scalability. Code and online appendices are available at [URL].
tldr: dSABRE is a new router for distributed quantum computers that minimizes EPR pair consumption by combining intra-core SWAP heuristics with inter-core teleportation scoring and proactive congestion relief.
motivation: EPR pair consumption is a critical resource in distributed quantum computing; existing routers like TeleSABRE and pytket-dqc are suboptimal. The goal is to reduce EPR usage to improve scalability and efficiency.
method: The algorithm iteratively resolves intra-core front-layer gates using SWAP scoring, then falls back to inter-core teleportation scoring with a five-term gate-centric score that includes a capacity-penalty term. It also includes a proactive congestion-relief pass and a BFS-layer construction for the inter-core extended set.
result: Across 18 MQT-Bench circuits at 25–64 qubits, dSABRE reduces geometric-mean EPR consumption by 41–44% over TeleSABRE and 16–68% over pytket-dqc. Scalability is demonstrated on QFT circuits up to 360 qubits.
conclusion: dSABRE significantly improves EPR efficiency in distributed quantum routing, with potential impact on quantum network design and resource management. Future work may extend to dynamic topologies or fault-tolerant settings.

title: Unified Entropy Entanglement
authors: Wenxue Ren, Binghao Li, Ruiqun Niu, Yu Guo, Shuanping Du
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The unified entropy as a promotion of the von Neumann entropy exhibits distinct diversity which contains the Tsallis entropy, the R\'{e}nyi entropy, the von Neumann entropy as special cases. The unified-([MATH]) entropy entanglement with [MATH] and [MATH] was shown to be an entanglement monotone in literature. In this paper, we explore unified-([MATH]) entropy entanglement with [MATH] and [MATH] and show that it is also an entanglement monotone and that both of them are monogamous. Going further, we present two kinds of global multipartite entanglement measures (GlMEMs) based on the unified entropy and each kind has two subclasses which are classified by the parameters [MATH] and [MATH]. Consequently, from the view of the complete multipartite entanglement measure theory, we show that one of them is a complete multipartite entanglement monotone and is not only completely monogamous but also tightly completely monogamous, but the other three are even not complete. We also explore the genuine entanglement measures induced by the unified entropy and the relations with the bipartite entanglement and the global entanglement are discussed, respectively.
tldr: This paper proves that unified-(q,r) entropy entanglement is an entanglement monotone and monogamous for certain parameter ranges, and introduces new global multipartite entanglement measures based on unified entropy.
motivation: To extend the study of unified entropy entanglement beyond previously known parameter ranges and to develop complete multipartite entanglement measures.
method: The authors use mathematical proofs to show monotonicity and monogamy of unified-(q,r) entropy entanglement for q>1 and 0<r<1, and define two kinds of global multipartite entanglement measures with subclasses based on parameters q and r.
result: One of the proposed global measures is a complete multipartite entanglement monotone and is tightly completely monogamous, while the other three are not complete. Genuine entanglement measures induced by unified entropy are also explored.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of multipartite entanglement measures by providing new tools based on unified entropy, with potential applications in quantum information theory.

title: Fidelity-Aware Frequency Allocation And Transpilation Co-Design For Tunable Coupler Quantum Systems
authors: Dylan Vanallen, Evan Mckinney, Israa G. Yusuf, Girgis Falstin, Gaurav Agarwal, Jason Pollack, Michael Hatridge, Alex K. Jones
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frequency crowding is a fundamental limitation in superconducting quantum architectures, particularly in tunable-coupler systems. We present a framework that explicitly models both coherent spectator-induced errors and incoherent lifetime effects through an error budgeting approach. Using this model, we analyze how frequency crowding impacts gate fidelity as module size and connectivity scale, and formulate a constrained optimization problem to assign qubit and coupler frequencies under realistic separation and hardware constraints. We demonstrate scalable frequency allocation strategies that minimize spectator-induced errors. We further show that increasing qubit count and coupling density within a module leads to a fidelity-connectivity tradeoff. To explore the benefits at the system scale, we have developed a noise-aware transpilation approach called FINESSE, which minimizes error by selecting high-fidelity paths that satisfy connectivity via SWAP insertion while jointly optimizing downstream gate execution. We demonstrate this physics-informed architecture-transpilation co-design approach for a SNAIL-based third-order coupler that natively realizes the [MATH] basis with frequency aware gate fidelities. On SNAIL architectures, FINESSE achieves an average 8.9% reduction in log-infidelity cost and 6.8% reduction in circuit depth vs. SABRE. We also compare results on IBM Brisbane's architecture.
tldr: A framework for frequency allocation and transpilation co-design to mitigate spectator errors in tunable-coupler superconducting quantum systems.
motivation: Frequency crowding limits gate fidelity in scalable superconducting quantum processors; existing approaches do not jointly optimize frequency assignment and circuit transpilation.
method: Develops an error budget model for coherent spectator-induced and incoherent lifetime errors, formulates a constrained optimization for frequency allocation, and introduces FINESSE, a noise-aware transpiler that selects high-fidelity paths with SWAP insertion.
result: FINESSE achieves 8.9% reduction in log-infidelity cost and 6.8% reduction in circuit depth compared to SABRE on SNAIL-based architectures.
conclusion: The co-design approach improves fidelity and scalability for tunable-coupler systems, with potential applications in larger quantum networks.

title: Photon Anomalous Blockade In Waveguide Cavity Qed With Atomic Mirrors
authors: Yang Xue, Yue Chang, Tao Shi, Yu-Xi Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Waveguide cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) with atomic mirrors is a growing research area of quantum optics and can be applied to quantum information processing. We here study the photon statistics of output fields from a waveguide cavity QED system, in which the waveguide is coupled to quantized mirror atoms and one driven medium atom. Our results show that the photon blockade can occur even for a bad atom cavity with large dissipation and small coupling between the medium atom and the cavity, in contrast to the small dissipation and the strong coupling of the medium atom to the cavity field for the conventional photon blockade or the quantum interference for the unconventional photon blockade in the cavity QED system. Utilizing both the master equation and scattering theories, we derive the condition under which the photon blockade occurs in weakly driven systems. We find that such photon anomalous blockade is due to the quantum Zeno effect and is robust against variations of the medium atom's position within the cavity. Our study paves a way to exploit the photon blockade and single-photon devices via the waveguide cavity QED.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a photon anomalous blockade in waveguide cavity QED with atomic mirrors, enabled by the quantum Zeno effect, which is robust against dissipation and atom position variations.
motivation: To achieve photon blockade in bad-cavity regimes where conventional blockade fails, enabling single-photon sources for quantum information processing.
method: The authors use master equation and scattering theory to analyze photon statistics of output fields from a waveguide cavity QED system with quantized mirror atoms and a driven medium atom.
result: Photon blockade occurs even with large dissipation and weak coupling, due to the quantum Zeno effect, and is robust to the medium atom's position.
conclusion: This work provides a new mechanism for photon blockade in waveguide QED, with potential applications in single-photon devices and quantum networks.

title: Multi-Modal Spectroscopy Theory For Ultrafast Control Of Rabi Oscillations
authors: J. W. Yu, H. B Wang, X. Q. Zhou, M. Tang, Z. B. Ni, X. T. Cheng, Y. Zhao, S. N Ding, J. Y. Yan, H. H. Zhu, C. H. Li, F. Liu, C. Y. Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a three-cavity scheme to realize full control of the emitter-cavity coupling strength in cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED). The involvement of coupled oscillators gives rise to transient dynamics comprising multiple spectral components, which significantly increases the numerical cost to resolve the fluorescence spectrum in the time domain. A generalized sensor method is hence developed to simplify the calculation process for the characterization of nonstationary quantum dynamics. Multi-modal spectroscopy reveals the emergence, splitting, and disappearance of supermodes in real time. Based on the depletion of the zero-energy supermode, ultrafast switching of Rabi oscillations is demonstrated for time-domain multi-modal spectroscopy. These results exhibit a consistent picture from the spectral control of multiple oscillators to the quantum observation in ultrafast dynamics, which establishes the sensor method as a powerful theoretical tool for the ultrafast spectroscopy of cQED systems.
tldr: A theoretical framework using a generalized sensor method to compute multi-modal fluorescence spectra in a three-cavity cQED system, enabling ultrafast control of Rabi oscillations.
motivation: To achieve full control of emitter-cavity coupling in cQED and to overcome the computational challenge of resolving time-domain fluorescence spectra with multiple spectral components.
method: Developed a generalized sensor method that simplifies the calculation of nonstationary quantum dynamics, applied to a three-cavity cQED system with coupled oscillators.
result: Multi-modal spectroscopy reveals real-time emergence, splitting, and disappearance of supermodes; ultrafast switching of Rabi oscillations is demonstrated via depletion of the zero-energy supermode.
conclusion: The sensor method provides a powerful theoretical tool for ultrafast spectroscopy of cQED systems, with potential applications in quantum control and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nonclassical Cutoff Fluctuations In Squeezed-Light-Driven High-Harmonic Generation
authors: Tsendsuren Khurelbaatar, R. T. Sang, Igor Litvinyuk
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong-field high-harmonic generation (HHG) is conventionally described semiclassically, with the driving laser treated as a classical field. This approximation becomes insufficient in nanoscale interaction geometries, where extreme spatial confinement raises the vacuum-field amplitude to the ~10^-2 level relative to the driving-field amplitude. When the quantum fluctuations of the driving field are redistributed between conjugate quadratures by squeezing, they can be directly imprinted onto macroscopic HHG observables. To model this interaction, we employ a Wigner phase-space approach that maps the quantum-optical driver onto a stochastic ensemble of time-dependent Schrodinger equation realizations. Although each realization remains classically simulable, the sub-vacuum quadrature covariance structure of squeezed states cannot be reproduced by any field admitting a non-negative Glauber-Sudarshan P-representation. Within this single-mode Gaussian framework, we show that amplitude squeezing suppresses the shot-to-shot variance of the HHG cutoff below the standard quantum limit (SQL). To leading order in the vacuum-to-driver ratio, the normalized cutoff variance decays exponentially with the squeezing parameter, independent of the absolute vacuum-field amplitude and therefore robust against uncertainties in the effective nanoscale mode volume. A subleading phase-noise contribution from the anti-squeezed quadrature produces a variance minimum near r_opt ~ 1.6, providing a concrete experimental target. These results establish the HHG cutoff variance ratio as a nonlinear, self-calibrating Heisenberg witness in which sub-SQL scaling directly reflects the redistribution of quantum uncertainty in the driving field.
tldr: This paper shows that squeezed-light-driven high-harmonic generation can exhibit sub-SQL cutoff fluctuations, serving as a Heisenberg witness of quantum uncertainty redistribution.
motivation: To explore how quantum fluctuations of the driving field, enhanced by squeezing, affect macroscopic HHG observables in nanoscale geometries where vacuum fluctuations are significant.
method: A Wigner phase-space approach maps the quantum-optical driver onto a stochastic ensemble of time-dependent Schrödinger equation realizations, each classically simulable but collectively capturing sub-vacuum quadrature covariance.
result: Amplitude squeezing suppresses the shot-to-shot variance of the HHG cutoff below the standard quantum limit, with exponential decay in squeezing parameter; a variance minimum occurs near r_opt ~ 1.6 due to anti-squeezed phase noise.
conclusion: The HHG cutoff variance ratio provides a nonlinear, self-calibrating Heisenberg witness, directly reflecting quantum uncertainty redistribution, with implications for quantum metrology and fundamental tests of quantum optics.

title: Realizing Tunable non-Hermitian Skin Effects In Dynamical Quantum Systems Via The Relative Phase Between Multiple Time-periodic Driving
authors: Huan-Yu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate how the relative phase between the multiple time periodic driving can decide the emergence and the favorable localization direction of non-Hermitian skin modes. For the static non-Hermitian quantum chain with parity time symmetry, non-Hermitian skin effects (NHSEs) can be prohibited. As the dynamical driving is turned on, NHSEs get artificially reactivated, where the relative phase can serve as the controlling switch by breaking the temporal symmetry constraints. Meanwhile, a change of relative phase can also alter the spatial structures of the long-time averaged effective Hamiltonian, which will consequently lead to the variation of skin localization direction for systems of higher dimensions. Our formalisms can be generally realized in diverse optical and mechanical platforms, and will pave the way for realizing tunable skin density profiles.
tldr: The relative phase between multiple time-periodic drives controls the emergence and direction of non-Hermitian skin effects in dynamical quantum systems.
motivation: To achieve tunable non-Hermitian skin effects (NHSE) in quantum systems, which are typically static and lack control over localization direction.
method: The authors study a parity-time symmetric non-Hermitian quantum chain under multiple time-periodic driving, using Floquet theory to derive the effective Hamiltonian and analyze the role of relative phase.
result: The relative phase can switch NHSE on/off and change the skin localization direction in higher dimensions, breaking temporal symmetry constraints.
conclusion: The formalism is generalizable to optical and mechanical platforms, enabling tunable skin density profiles for applications in sensing and wave manipulation.

title: Sensitivity Evaluation Of Su(1,1) Interferometers With Arbitrary Input Probe State And Homodyne Detections
authors: Sonu Jana, Dhruv Baheti, Paul Grossiord, Fabien Bretenaker, Nadia Belabas, Syamsundar de
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a general theoretical derivation of the phase sensitivity achieved by SU(1,1) interferometers under homodyne detection. The general expressions obtained accommodate arbitrary input states and include internal and external losses. In this systematic review, both full SU(1,1) interferometers with two parametric amplifiers and the truncated interferometers with only one parametric amplifier are examined. We investigate scenarios involving both single-output ports and joint homodyne detection, and consider parametric amplifiers with equal gains or with a boosted gain second amplifier. Our analytical formulation provides physical insight and understanding of the improvements in the sensitivity, which are shown to originate from noise reduction and/or signal amplification, depending on the configurations and practical implementations. Surprisingly, the configuration with single-output mode detection and parametric amplifiers with equal gains exhibits the highest robustness to very high internal losses. We finally apply this framework to a ubiquitous [MATH] input two-mode coherent probe state. This approach permits the comparison of different strategies and the optimization of the interferometer performance in the presence of losses. In particular, we determine which amplification and detection configurations provide the best performance, depending on the level of losses. This exemplifies how this general analytical approach provides a powerful tool to design quantum-enhanced interferometers and achieve optimal sensitivity with selected probe states and homodyne detection.
tldr: This paper provides a general theoretical framework for phase sensitivity in SU(1,1) interferometers with arbitrary input states and homodyne detection, including loss effects.
motivation: To understand and optimize the performance of SU(1,1) interferometers for quantum-enhanced metrology, particularly in the presence of losses.
method: Analytical derivation of phase sensitivity expressions for full and truncated SU(1,1) interferometers with homodyne detection, considering arbitrary input states, internal/external losses, and various detection configurations.
result: The configuration with single-output mode detection and equal-gain parametric amplifiers shows highest robustness to high internal losses; the framework allows comparison and optimization of different strategies.
conclusion: The general analytical approach provides a powerful tool for designing quantum-enhanced interferometers and achieving optimal sensitivity with selected probe states and homodyne detection.

title: Computable Lower Bound Of The Parameterized Entanglement Monotone
authors: Ning Yang, Yu Guo, Shuanping Du
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although numerous measures of entanglement have been proposed so far, the calculation of a given faithful entanglement measure is a hard work since it is always involved in some optimization process. It is, therefore, important to estimate the lower bound of a given entanglement measure for an arbitrary quantum state. This results in a subject of intensive mathematical research. In particular, along this line, the lower bounds of concurrence or other measures that are induced from concurrence have been explored a lot. Here, we investigate the lower bounds of two kinds of entanglement monotones, i.e., [MATH]-concurrence ([MATH]) and [MATH]-concurrence ([MATH]), or termed the parameterized entanglement monotone together. We obtain, in the light of the informationally complete ([MATH], [MATH])-positive operator-valued measure [([MATH], [MATH])-POVM], the lower bounds for the case of [MATH], [MATH] for two-qudit states, and the case of [MATH] for two-qubit states. We list several examples which show that the lower bounds based on ([MATH], [MATH])-POVM outperform that of GSIC-POVM and SIC-POVM, and all these measurement based bounds are better then the ones induced by positive partial transpose (PPT) and realignment criteria in literature. In addition, we obtain an analytical formula of the parameterized entanglement monotone with [MATH] and [MATH] for the isotropic state.
tldr: The paper derives computable lower bounds for parameterized entanglement monotones (λ-concurrence and μ-concurrence) using (α, β)-POVMs, outperforming existing bounds.
motivation: Calculating faithful entanglement measures is computationally hard due to optimization; thus, finding tight lower bounds is important for practical entanglement quantification.
method: The authors use informationally complete (α, β)-POVMs to derive lower bounds for λ-concurrence and μ-concurrence for two-qudit and two-qubit states, and compare them with bounds from GSIC-POVM, SIC-POVM, PPT, and realignment criteria.
result: The (α, β)-POVM-based bounds are tighter than those from GSIC-POVM, SIC-POVM, PPT, and realignment criteria. An analytical formula for the parameterized entanglement monotone for isotropic states is also obtained.
conclusion: The work provides practical tools for estimating entanglement in arbitrary states, with potential applications in quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: GeneCS: Synthesizing Resource-Efficient Code Surgery For Arbitrary Quantum Stabilizer Codes
authors: Junyu Zhou, Ali Javadi-Abhari, Gushu Li
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficiently realizing logical operations on general stabilizer codes remains a long-standing challenge in fault tolerant quantum computing. While code surgery provides a general framework with provable guarantees by joint logical measurements, existing constructions are largely theoretical and incur substantial ancilla overhead in practice. In this work, we propose GeneCS, a resource-efficient compiler for synthesizing code surgery protocols for arbitrary stabilizer codes. Our approach leverages structure-aware optimizations to eliminate redundancy in graph construction, dynamically balance expansion and congestion, and incorporate code degree constraints. Experimental results show that GeneCS achieves an average reduction of over [MATH] in ancillary qubits and checks for both single-code and cross-code logical operations, while preserving logical error rates. Moreover, our compiler scales to codes with more than [MATH] qubits with an amortized compilation time of about one second per instance. These results enable practical logical operations and efficient cross-code communication, thereby supporting the deployment of modern QLDPC codes and heterogeneous quantum architectures.
tldr: GeneCS is a compiler that synthesizes resource-efficient code surgery protocols for arbitrary stabilizer codes, reducing ancilla qubits and checks while preserving logical error rates.
motivation: Existing code surgery constructions for fault-tolerant quantum computing incur substantial ancilla overhead, hindering practical deployment of logical operations and cross-code communication.
method: The authors propose structure-aware optimizations including redundancy elimination in graph construction, dynamic balancing of expansion and congestion, and incorporation of code degree constraints.
result: GeneCS achieves an average reduction in ancillary qubits and checks for both single-code and cross-code logical operations, scales to codes with over 1000 qubits, and has amortized compilation time of about one second per instance.
conclusion: This work enables practical logical operations and efficient cross-code communication, supporting deployment of modern QLDPC codes and heterogeneous quantum architectures.

title: Zero-level $ccz$ Distillation
authors: Tomohiro Itogawa, Yutaka Hirano, Yutaro Akahoshi, Keisuke Fujii
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magic state distillation is a key component of fault-tolerant quantum computation, as it enables the implementation of non-Clifford gates such as the [MATH] gate and the [MATH] gate via gate teleportation. However, conventional distillation protocols require a large number of logical qubits and introduce substantial spatial and temporal overhead, posing a significant bottleneck for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation. In this work, we propose a zero-level distillation protocol that efficiently generates a high-fidelity logical [MATH] magic state using only physical qubits on a two-dimensional square lattice with nearest-neighbor interactions. Our method leverages the transversal [MATH] operation of the [MATH] code to fault-tolerantly encode the state [MATH], which is subsequently teleported to three surface-code logical qubits via lattice surgery. To enable teleportation between codes with different distances, we introduce adaptively initialized teleportation (AIT), a tailored initialization procedure for the surface code. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the logical error rate scales as [MATH] with respect to the physical error rate [MATH]. For example, the proposed method improves the logical error rate by approximately one and two orders of magnitude at [MATH] and [MATH], respectively, compared to conventional seven-[MATH]-gate approaches. The distillation circuit requires only 22 physical qubits, 3 logical qubits, and a circuit depth of 24, reducing the space-time overhead by a factor of approximately 5-10 compared to previous methods. This result highlights the practicality of [MATH]-state distillation in early fault-tolerant quantum computation and offers a new direction toward resource-efficient physical-level magic state distillation beyond conventional [MATH]-state generation.
tldr: Proposes a zero-level magic state distillation protocol for the CCZ gate using only physical qubits on a 2D square lattice, significantly reducing space-time overhead.
motivation: Conventional magic state distillation requires many logical qubits and large overhead, hindering scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation. This work aims to reduce resource requirements for early fault-tolerant devices.
method: Leverages the transversal CCZ operation of the [[8,3,2]] code to fault-tolerantly encode the CCZ state, then teleports it to three surface-code logical qubits via lattice surgery, introducing adaptively initialized teleportation (AIT) for codes with different distances.
result: Logical error rate scales as O(p^2) with physical error rate p; improves logical error rate by 1-2 orders of magnitude over conventional seven-gate approaches; uses only 22 physical qubits, 3 logical qubits, and circuit depth 24, reducing space-time overhead by factor 5-10.
conclusion: Demonstrates practical CCZ-state distillation for early fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering a resource-efficient path beyond conventional magic state generation.

title: Building Europe's Quantum Shield: The Strategic View For A Continent-Wide Quantum Key Ditribution (qkd) Infrastructure
authors: Leandros Maglaras, Ilias Papastamatiou, Alexios Aivaliotis, Evangelos Markatos, Konstantinos Karantzalos
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fast growth of quantum computing can lead to amazing scientific breakthroughs while on the same time can be used to break today's security systems, raising new risks for existing digital systems. Facing this challenge, the European's Union's deployement of the European Communication Infrastructure (EuroQCI) is crucial. The SEEWQCI project combines fiber cables, satellite communications and enhanced security rules to build a strong digital shield. Its focus is to protect vital services like power grids and hospitals keeping Europeans' data safe.
tldr: This paper outlines the strategic deployment of a continent-wide Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) infrastructure in Europe, focusing on the EuroQCI and SEEWQCI projects.
motivation: The rapid advancement of quantum computing threatens current cryptographic systems, necessitating the development of quantum-safe communication networks to protect critical infrastructure.
method: The paper presents a strategic overview of the EuroQCI initiative and the SEEWQCI project, which integrates fiber-optic cables, satellite links, and enhanced security protocols to build a pan-European QKD network.
result: The proposed infrastructure aims to secure vital services such as power grids and hospitals by distributing quantum keys, thereby safeguarding European data against future quantum threats.
conclusion: The deployment of a continent-wide QKD network is crucial for Europe's digital security, and the SEEWQCI project serves as a model for integrating multiple technologies to achieve quantum-safe communication.

title: Journey In Quantum Metrology And Sensing From Foundations To Applications: A Review
authors: Priya Ghosh, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Debraj Rakshit, Aditi Sen De, Ujjwal Sen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a review on quantum metrology and sensing, from its foundations to current applications. Highlights of the review include consideration of both frequentist and Bayesian approaches to parameter estimation; single as well as multiparameter estimation; estimation for different encoding processes comprising unitary as well as noisy channels, quantum thermometry, and channels involving indefinite causal order; different estimation strategies incorporating also recent advances like quantum error correction-aided methods and reservoir engineering; usefulness of quantum Fisher information to detect resources; applications of quantum metrology in diverse arenas covering quantum many-body sensors, sensing protocols in atomic ensembles, atom-photon systems, and continuous-variable systems, quantum imaging, quantum illumination, atomic clocks and atom interferometry, etc; and experimental realizations of quantum sensors in different physical platforms.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum metrology and sensing covering foundations, frequentist and Bayesian estimation, multiparameter estimation, noisy channels, and applications in many-body systems, atomic ensembles, and quantum imaging.
motivation: To provide a broad overview of the field of quantum metrology and sensing, from theoretical foundations to experimental implementations, for researchers and newcomers.
method: The paper is a review that surveys key concepts, methods, and results in quantum metrology, including Fisher information, estimation strategies, encoding processes, and experimental platforms.
result: The review highlights the breadth of quantum metrology, including quantum error correction, reservoir engineering, indefinite causal order, and applications in quantum many-body sensors, atomic clocks, and quantum illumination.
conclusion: Quantum metrology is a mature field with diverse applications; future directions may include further integration with quantum error correction and exploration of complex quantum systems.

title: Klein Tunneling Of The Laser Coherence
authors: Konstantin Manannikov, Sagie Gadasi, Ekaterina Mironova, Eran Bernstein, Andrei Poliakov, Nir Davidson, Alexander N. Poddubny
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study theoretically the lasing synchronization of the two arrays of lasers with the complex mode dispersion, separated by a spectrally detuned barrier. We demonstrate that for lasing at the Dirac point, the synchronization persists for an order of magnitude higher barriers than in the arrays with a usual parabolic dispersion or a purely dissipative coupling. We interpret this effect as the Klein tunneling of the laser coherence through the barrier. Our numerical findings are supported by an analysis of the delocalization of the linearized eigenmodes of the arrays, which enhances the synchronization.
tldr: The paper studies lasing synchronization in laser arrays with complex mode dispersion, showing enhanced synchronization at the Dirac point due to Klein tunneling of laser coherence.
motivation: To understand how synchronization in laser arrays can be improved beyond conventional parabolic dispersion or dissipative coupling, potentially enabling robust coherent light sources.
method: Theoretical analysis of two laser arrays separated by a spectrally detuned barrier, using linearized eigenmode delocalization and numerical simulations.
result: Synchronization persists for order-of-magnitude higher barriers at the Dirac point compared to parabolic dispersion, attributed to Klein tunneling of laser coherence.
conclusion: The findings suggest that Dirac-like dispersion can greatly enhance synchronization, with implications for designing robust laser arrays and possibly for quantum coherence phenomena.

title: Q-PhotoNAS: Hybrid Quantum Neural Architecture Search Framework On Photonic Devices
authors: Farah Elnakhal, Alberto Marchisio, Nouhaila Innan, Gabriel Falcao, Muhammad Shafique
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic quantum computing is a promising platform for scalable quantum machine learning, but designing effective hybrid architectures remains challenging under hardware and optimization constraints. Existing approaches rely on manually tuned architectures that fail to account for the collaboration between classical preprocessing, phase encoding, and photonic circuit structure, limiting both accuracy and hardware compatibility. In this paper, we propose a neural architecture search framework for hybrid photonic quantum-classical models that combines genetic algorithm-based search with learnable quantum phase encoding to systematically explore the joint design space of classical and quantum components. Our framework encodes 19 hyperparameters across six gene groups and evolves a population of hybrid architectures using group-based crossover, per-gene mutation, and elitism, evaluating each candidate on a short training budget before full retraining of the best found design. We evaluate our framework on two image classification benchmarks, Digits and MNIST, achieving final validation accuracies of 99.44% and 98.78%, respectively, with first-principles execution time estimates on the Quandela Ascella photonic QPU projecting single-image inference at 67 ms (Digits) and 149 ms (MNIST). Our quantum contribution analysis further shows that the photonic layer extracts non-redundant features orthogonal to the classical pathway, providing a measurable accuracy advantage over classical-only baselines. Our results demonstrate that automated architecture search is both practical and impactful for hybrid photonic systems, opening the way for systematic design space exploration of quantum AI on photonic devices.
tldr: A neural architecture search framework for hybrid photonic quantum-classical models is proposed, achieving high accuracy on image classification benchmarks.
motivation: Manually designed hybrid photonic architectures often fail to optimize the collaboration between classical preprocessing, phase encoding, and photonic circuit structure, limiting accuracy and hardware compatibility.
method: A genetic algorithm-based search with learnable quantum phase encoding explores a joint design space of 19 hyperparameters across six gene groups, evaluating candidates on a short training budget before full retraining.
result: Final validation accuracies of 99.44% (Digits) and 98.78% (MNIST) are achieved, with single-image inference times of 67 ms and 149 ms on a photonic QPU; quantum contribution analysis shows the photonic layer extracts non-redundant features.
conclusion: Automated architecture search is practical for hybrid photonic systems, enabling systematic design space exploration for quantum AI on photonic devices.

title: Single-pump Hybrid Nonlinearities In Transparent Conductors
authors: Wallace Jaffray, Sven Stengel, Alexandra Boltasseva, Vladimir M. Shalaev, Carlo Rizza, Domenico de Ceglia, Maria Antonietta Vincenti, Michael Scalora, Matteo Clerici, Marcello Ferrera
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-index transparent conducting oxides have attracted significant attention because ultrafast optical excitation in these materials can induce exceptionally large temporal index gradients. Due to this remarkable nonlinear optical behaviour, this material platform enables sub-picosecond, all-optical control of photon energy and momentum, with growing relevance for integrated photonics, quantum optics, and optical computation. Owing to their hybrid electronic structure, transparent conductors exhibit both intraband and interband nonlinearities, previously accessed using dual-colour excitation with near-infrared and ultraviolet pumps. Here, we show that both excitation regimes can be activated using a single, intense near-infrared pump. Above a threshold intensity, the pump drives hot-electron intraband dynamics while simultaneously generating higher harmonics that trigger interband excitation. The interplay of these two effects sharpens the temporal features of the recorded transmissivity which in turn substantially broadens the effective material bandwidth. Finally, by comparing linear and circular pumping conditions, we further demonstrate that the observed interband nonlinearities originate from harmonic generation rather than from direct multiphoton absorption. Our results provide key insights into the strong-field optical response in these time-varying photonic materials, opening new frontiers for the ultra-fast manipulation of photons in both classic and quantum regimes.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that a single intense near-infrared pump can activate both intraband and interband nonlinearities in transparent conducting oxides via harmonic generation, enabling ultrafast all-optical control.
motivation: To understand and exploit the hybrid electronic structure of transparent conductors for ultrafast photonic applications, particularly for all-optical control of light.
method: Experimental and theoretical study of nonlinear optical response in transparent conducting oxides under intense near-infrared pumping, comparing linear and circular polarization to distinguish harmonic generation from multiphoton absorption.
result: Above a threshold intensity, the pump drives hot-electron intraband dynamics and simultaneously generates higher harmonics that trigger interband excitation, sharpening temporal features and broadening the effective material bandwidth.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into strong-field optical response in time-varying photonic materials, opening new possibilities for ultrafast manipulation of photons in classical and quantum regimes.

title: Statistical Interpretation Of The Procedures Measurement Of Physical Quantities
authors: Pandiscia Carlo
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work develops a conceptual framework for the foundations of quantum physics, linking two main approaches: the algebraic formulation and quantum probability. Rather than proposing new axioms or theories, the text reorganizes and synthesizes existing models, highlighting their assumptions, conceptual structures, and operational significance. The analysis begins with von Neumann's measurement theory and its subsequent developments by Mackey, emphasizing the role of experimentally feasible procedures and the need for a statistical model grounded in laboratory practice. The work adopts an operational perspective, according to which physical quantities are defined solely through experimental measurement methods, and the corresponding probabilistic measures are derived from measurement outcomes. The introduction critically examines the limitations of purely mathematical formulations - such as the algebraic method - when separated from experimental interpretation. The text argues for a clear distinction between axioms, postulates, and presuppositions, and for a reconstruction of quantum theory that respects both empirical constraints and conceptual clarity. Overall, the goal is to provide a coherent path from operational principles to algebraic structures, offering a basis for an axiomatic reformulation of quantum mechanics that remains faithful to physical practice.
tldr: The paper develops a conceptual framework linking algebraic formulation and quantum probability, focusing on operational definitions of measurement and statistical interpretation.
motivation: To address limitations of purely mathematical formulations of quantum theory when separated from experimental interpretation, and to provide a coherent path from operational principles to algebraic structures.
method: Conceptual analysis and synthesis of existing models, including von Neumann's measurement theory and Mackey's developments, with an operational perspective.
result: A framework that reorganizes and synthesizes existing models, highlighting assumptions and operational significance, but no new empirical results or formal theorems.
conclusion: The work offers a basis for an axiomatic reformulation of quantum mechanics that respects empirical constraints, but remains at the conceptual level without direct experimental or computational implications.

title: Matrix Product Operator Encodings Of The Magnus Expansion And Dyson Series
authors: Victor Vanthilt, Maarten van Damme, Jutho Haegeman, Ian P. Mcculloch, Laurens Vanderstraeten
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a matrix product operator (MPO) encoding of the Magnus expansion and the Dyson series for one-dimensional quantum lattice models with time-dependent Hamiltonians. The MPO construction can be made accurate up to arbitrary order in the time step, it can be applied to both finite and infinite systems, and it can handle long-range interactions. The resulting MPO can be combined with state-of-the-art time evolution algorithms based on matrix product states, allowing for drastic improvements in simulating evolution under time-dependent Hamiltonians. Our MPO construction can also be used for the optimization of quantum circuits in the context of quantum simulation of time-dependent Hamiltonians.
tldr: This paper introduces MPO encodings of the Magnus expansion and Dyson series for simulating time-dependent quantum lattice models, focusing on algorithmic efficiency rather than the user's specific interests.
motivation: To improve simulation of time-dependent Hamiltonians in 1D quantum lattice models by leveraging matrix product operators.
method: Constructs MPO representations of the Magnus expansion and Dyson series up to arbitrary order, applicable to finite and infinite systems with long-range interactions.
result: The MPO encoding enables more efficient time evolution algorithms for matrix product states, with potential for quantum circuit optimization.
conclusion: The method offers a systematic way to simulate time-dependent Hamiltonians, but its direct relevance to information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, communication, or hybrid quantum systems is limited.

title: What We Talk About When We Talk About Dissipative Quantum Chaos
authors: Lucas S\'a, Pedro Ribeiro, Sergey Denisov
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dissipative quantum chaos is an emerging theory that is expected to extend the ideas, concepts, and methodology of conventional Hamiltonian quantum chaos from coherent evolution to open quantum dynamics. The new theory should provide a set of tools to distinguish chaotic open quantum systems from integrable ones, as well as quantitative measures of their chaoticity (or, conversely, integrability). The foundations of this theory were laid in the late 1980s, and from the very start it was clear that, like its Hamiltonian predecessor, it had to be based on the spectral properties of the operators governing open quantum evolution. After these first steps, the field remained relatively quiet for many years and it is only over the last decade that the development of dissipative quantum chaos has received a strong boost, as confirmed by a large number of publications on this topic and, very recently, the first experiments performed to test its theoretical predictions. In this chapter, we review these recent developments and outline the basic foundations of dissipative quantum chaos.
tldr: This paper reviews the foundations and recent developments of dissipative quantum chaos, a theory extending Hamiltonian quantum chaos to open quantum systems.
motivation: To consolidate and advance the understanding of chaotic behavior in open quantum systems, which has seen renewed interest and experimental tests in the last decade.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical developments, spectral analysis of Lindbladians, and connections to random matrix theory and many-body physics.
result: It outlines the basic foundations, recent theoretical progress, and first experimental verifications of dissipative quantum chaos.
conclusion: The field is maturing, with potential applications in understanding thermalization, quantum information processing, and nonequilibrium dynamics, but direct links to the user's specific interests are not evident.

title: Balancing Quasi-Bragg Regime And Velocity Selectivity In Quantum-Enhanced Atom Interferometry
authors: Christian Miguel Karres (technical University Of Darmstadt, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz), Daniel Derr (technical University Of Darmstadt), Enno Giese
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin squeezing in atomic ensembles enables atom interferometry with sensitivities below the shot-noise limit, but the associated entanglement is highly susceptible to loss, making imperfections in atom optics a central limitation. Bragg diffraction is an established technique for driving transitions between atomic momentum states and enables large-momentum transfer through higher-order diffraction while preserving the internal state. However, it is intrinsically limited by two competing mechanisms: short light pulses induce parasitic diffraction into off-resonant orders beyond an effective two-level description, while long pulses face velocity selectivity. We derive analytical expressions in a second-quantized framework for the atom optics and phase uncertainty of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer including these effects. We demonstrate that sub-shot-noise scaling is achieved only in a regime of intermediate pulse duration. Furthermore, we show that deleterious effects of higher-order diffraction are partially mitigated by optimizing the input quantum state.
tldr: This paper analyzes the trade-off between quasi-Bragg diffraction and velocity selectivity in quantum-enhanced atom interferometry, showing that sub-shot-noise scaling requires intermediate pulse durations.
