A centralized offline benchmark is also provided for performance comparison. Numerical results show that the proposed distributed design achieves performance close to the centralized benchmark under different interference conditions, while maintaining favorable scalability as the network size increases.
tldr: This paper proposes a distributed two-timescale optimization framework for multi-cell 6DMA networks to manage inter-cell interference via joint precoder and antenna rotation design.
motivation: To address the coupled antenna rotation and precoder design across base stations in multi-cell 6DMA systems for improved downlink performance under inter-cell interference.
method: Formulates a weighted sum-rate maximization problem and solves it with a distributed two-timescale algorithm using inter-cell interference power constraint coordination, edge-wise IPC via grid search and random maximal matching, and a centralized benchmark.
result: The distributed design achieves performance close to the centralized benchmark with favorable scalability as network size increases.
conclusion: The proposed approach enables scalable interference management in multi-cell 6DMA networks, with potential for practical deployment.

title: Data-Driven Reduced Modeling Of Delayed Dynamical Systems Via Spectral Submanifolds
authors: Giacomo Abbasciano, Gergely Buza, George Haller
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how the recent extension of spectral submanifold (SSM) theory to delay differential equations (DDEs) enables data-driven model reduction of nonlinear delay systems. First, using a scalar DDE with a single discrete delay, we compare equation-based and data-driven SSM reductions, to illustrate the need for the latter. We then use the same algorithm to obtain purely data-driven, SSM-reduced, delay-free ODE models for several nonlinear delayed systems. Our approach requires no information about the form of the underlying DDE, or about the number and magnitude of the delays it contains. Our SSM-reduced, low-dimensional models remain predictive even for chaotic dynamics. We also illustrate the use of parametric SSM-reduction to capture bifurcations in systems with both distributed and discrete delays. Finally we extend the theoretical underpinning of delayed SSM-reductions to non-autonomous systems with periodic delays, and apply these results to experimental data from a control system with feedback delay and quantization.
tldr: This paper develops data-driven reduced-order models for delayed dynamical systems using spectral submanifold theory, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, or related topics.
motivation: To enable model reduction of nonlinear delay systems without prior knowledge of the delay structure, which is common in engineering and biological systems.
method: Extends spectral submanifold (SSM) theory to delay differential equations (DDEs) and applies data-driven algorithms to construct low-dimensional ODE models from time-series data.
result: SSM-reduced models accurately predict dynamics, including chaos, for several nonlinear delayed systems, and parametric SSM-reduction captures bifurcations. The method also works for non-autonomous systems with periodic delays and experimental data.
conclusion: Data-driven SSM reduction is a powerful tool for simplifying delayed systems, with potential applications in control and experimental settings, but is unrelated to quantum computing or information thermodynamics.

title: From PDEs Constrained Optimization To Controllability Problems Via Time Domain Decomposition
authors: Liu-Di Lu Pierre-Henri Cocquet
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper focuses on the application of time domain decomposition to solve partial differential equations constrained optimization problems and controllability problems. After clarifying the link between these two types of problems, we show that applying time domain decomposition to both problems leads to the same convergence behavior. Our numerical experiments also confirm these theoretical findings.
tldr: This paper applies time domain decomposition to PDE-constrained optimization and controllability problems, showing they converge similarly.
motivation: To unify the treatment of PDE-constrained optimization and controllability problems using time domain decomposition.
method: Theoretical analysis linking the two problem types and numerical experiments demonstrating convergence behavior.
result: Time domain decomposition leads to the same convergence behavior for both optimization and controllability problems.
conclusion: The approach provides a unified framework, but implications for quantum or information thermodynamics are not discussed.

title: Schwarz Modulus Based Matrix Splittings With Minimal Polynomial Extrapolation Acceleration For Linear Complementarity Problems Arising From American Option Pricing
authors: Martin J. Gande, Si-Wei Liao, Liu-Di Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pricing American options is more complicated than pricing European options, because they can be exercised at any time, and one thus needs to solve a linear complementarity problem instead of simply doing time stepping for computing European options. We introduce a new Schwarz modulus-based splitting method for solving such linear complementarity problems, and further accelerate them using Modified Polynomial Extrapolation, a non-linear vector sequence acceleration technique, which is very much related to Krylov methods in the linear case. Numerical experiments on a model problem show that our new solver can have close to an order of magnitude lower iteration counts than the classically used modulus-based matrix splitting technique.
tldr: This paper introduces a Schwarz modulus-based matrix splitting method accelerated by minimal polynomial extrapolation for solving linear complementarity problems in American option pricing.
motivation: American option pricing requires solving linear complementarity problems, which are computationally intensive; existing modulus-based methods have high iteration counts.
method: The authors propose a new Schwarz modulus-based splitting method and accelerate it using Modified Polynomial Extrapolation, a nonlinear vector sequence acceleration technique related to Krylov methods.
result: Numerical experiments show that the new solver achieves nearly an order of magnitude lower iteration counts compared to classical modulus-based matrix splitting techniques.
conclusion: The method offers significant computational savings for American option pricing, with potential extensions to other linear complementarity problems.

title: Incentive-Aligned Vehicle-to-Vehicle Energy Trading Via Nash-Integrated Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yujin Lin, Yue Yang, Hao Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) energy trading enables decentralized peer-to-peer energy exchange among electric vehicles (EVs), reducing grid dependency while monetizing surplus capacity. However, coordinating self-interested EV agents with diverse charging needs and uncertain arrival-departure schedules remains challenging. Existing approaches either require centralized optimization with computational limitations or lack fairness guarantees. This paper integrates Nash Bargaining Solution into Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient, namely Nash-MADDPG, for incentive-aligned V2V energy trading. Nash bargaining determines efficient bilateral pricing, while Nash-guided price proximity rewards align agent learning toward bargaining-optimal strategies. Evaluation over 30-day continuous operation demonstrates an improvement of 61.6% in social welfare and 62.9% improvement in trading volume over Double Auction, while achieving superior fairness, such as 40.1% improvement in Jain's index. Testing across 6-100 agents over a 30-day horizon with continuous vehicle turnover confirms scalability across population size and empirically stable pricing near the Nash Bargaining benchmark.
tldr: This paper proposes a Nash-integrated multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for vehicle-to-vehicle energy trading, focusing on incentive alignment and fairness.
motivation: Existing V2V energy trading methods either require centralized optimization or lack fairness guarantees, motivating the need for a decentralized, incentive-aligned approach.
method: The authors integrate Nash Bargaining Solution into Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (Nash-MADDPG) to determine efficient bilateral pricing and guide agent learning via Nash-guided price proximity rewards.
result: Over 30-day simulations, Nash-MADDPG improves social welfare by 61.6%, trading volume by 62.9%, and fairness (Jain's index) by 40.1% compared to Double Auction, with scalability from 6 to 100 agents.
conclusion: The framework demonstrates effective decentralized coordination and stable pricing, suggesting potential for real-world V2V energy markets, though further validation on physical systems is needed.

title: Density Of Neural Network Classes On Compact Subsets Of Topological Vector Spaces
authors: Arash Ghorbanalizadeh Mohammad Javad Baghbanbashi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove density results for neural-network classes on compact sets \(K\subset X\), where \(X\) is a topological vector space whose continuous dual \(X^*\) separates points. Let \(\Psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be a continuous squashing function. We show that the class \[ \Sigma_X(\Psi) = \left\{ \sum_{j=1}^{N}\omega_j\Psi(f_j(x)+b_j): N\in\mathbb N,\ \omega_j,b_j\in\mathbb R,\ f_j\in X^* \right\} \] is dense in \(C(K)\) with respect to the uniform norm. As a consequence, if \(\mu\) is a Radon probability measure supported on \(K\), then \(\Sigma_X(\Psi)\) is dense in \(L^p(K,\mu)\) for every \(1\le p<\infty\).
tldr: This paper proves density theorems for neural network classes on compact subsets of topological vector spaces, showing that certain neural network architectures can approximate continuous functions uniformly.
motivation: To extend universal approximation theorems for neural networks from Euclidean spaces to more general topological vector spaces, thereby broadening the theoretical foundation of neural network expressivity.
method: The authors consider a class of neural networks with a continuous squashing activation function and linear functionals from the continuous dual as weights, and prove density in C(K) using functional analysis and approximation theory.
result: The class Σ_X(Ψ) is dense in C(K) with respect to the uniform norm, and consequently dense in L^p(K, μ) for any Radon probability measure μ on K.
conclusion: The results provide a general framework for universal approximation in topological vector spaces, with potential applications in machine learning and functional analysis.

title: Chain Reactions: How Nonce Collisions In Ecdsa Compromise Polygon Mev Searchers
authors: Yash Madhwal, Andrey Seoev, Raffaele Della Pietra, Anastasiia Smirnova, Yury Yanovich
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ECDSA signatures form the bedrock of blockchain transaction authentication, yet their security critically depends on proper nonce generation. We uncover a critical vulnerability in the Polygon MEV ecosystem: systematic nonce reuse that enables complete private key recovery. Analyzing on-chain data reveals that searchers, driven by the need for sub-second response times in sealed-bid auctions, employ predictable nonce patterns. These patterns create linear relationships between signatures, allowing passive attackers to recover private keys using elementary algebra. We provide a compact linear-system formulation for such attacks, including the dangerous case of cross-wallet nonce collisions, and present concrete evidence of exploitable patterns on Polygon. Our findings demonstrate how protocol-induced latency pressures can lead to catastrophic cryptographic failures in production blockchain systems, where a single implementation error compromises multiple accounts simultaneously.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonce reuse vulnerabilities in ECDSA signatures within the Polygon MEV ecosystem, enabling private key recovery.
motivation: To uncover and demonstrate a critical cryptographic vulnerability in blockchain transaction authentication due to predictable nonce generation.
method: Analysis of on-chain data to identify nonce patterns; formulation of linear-system attacks for private key recovery.
result: Systematic nonce reuse by Polygon MEV searchers allows passive attackers to recover private keys using elementary algebra.
conclusion: Protocol-induced latency pressures can lead to catastrophic cryptographic failures; highlights need for secure nonce generation in blockchain systems.

title: Resource Bounded Ku\v{c}era-G\'{a}cs Theorems
authors: Satyadev Nandakumar, Akhil S, Chandra Shekhar Tiwari
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Kuera--G\'{a}cs theorem is a fundamental result in algorithmic randomness. It states that every infinite sequence [MATH] is Turing reducible to a Martin-L\"of random [MATH]. This paper studies resource-bounded analogues of the Kuera-G\'acs Theorem, at the resource bounds of polynomial-time and finite-state computation. We prove a {quasi-polynomial-time}{ Kuera-G\'acs Theorem}, showing that every infinite sequence [MATH] is quasi-polynomial-time reducible to a sequence [MATH]. We also show that for any [MATH], the oracle use of [MATH] is [MATH] bits for obtaining the first [MATH] bits of [MATH]. We then study the relationship between compressibility and Turing reductions, in the polynomial-time setting. We establish that [MATH], demonstrating that the lower polynomial-time Turing decompression ratio is precisely characterized by the polynomial-time Kolmogorov complexity rate. We note that this characterization fails for the polynomial-time dimension if one-way functions exist, resolving an open problem from Doty's work. We use these results to strengthen the {quasi-polynomial-time}{ Kuera-G\'acs Theorem}. We show that every infinite sequence [MATH] is quasi-polynomial-time reducible to a {polynomial-time random} sequence [MATH], where the lower oracle use rate of the reduction is less than [MATH]. We also show that any sequence extracted from the (even larger) set of by a finite-state reduction must have a convergent asymptotic frequency for its symbols. Since sequences lacking this invariant property exist, they cannot be finite-state reduced from any normal sequence. Hence we show that the Kuera-G\'acs theorem for finite-state reductions.
tldr: This paper proves resource-bounded versions of the Kučera–Gács theorem in algorithmic randomness, focusing on quasi-polynomial-time and finite-state reductions.
motivation: To understand the trade-offs between computational resources and randomness in the context of Turing reducibility, and to resolve open problems about polynomial-time decompression and dimension.
method: The authors use techniques from algorithmic information theory, Kolmogorov complexity, and computational complexity to construct reductions and analyze oracle use rates.
result: They prove a quasi-polynomial-time Kučera–Gács theorem, characterize polynomial-time Turing decompression ratio via Kolmogorov complexity, and show that finite-state reductions from normal sequences force convergent asymptotic frequencies.
conclusion: The results deepen the understanding of resource-bounded randomness and reducibility, but the paper is purely theoretical and not directly applicable to the user's research interests.

title: Sentil: A Runtime Verification Tool For Probabilistic Temporal Logic
authors: Ernest Bonnah Paapa Kwesi Quansah
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic cyber-physical systems (CPS) permeate critical infrastructure, from autonomous vehicles to medical devices. Yet, tools for runtime verification of such systems capturing the probabilistic dynamics in stochastic systems remain generally absent despite theoretical foundations established nearly a decade ago. In this paper, we present SENTIL, a novel runtime verification tool with provable statistical guarantees for the runtime monitoring of requirements expressed as Probabilistic Signal Temporal Logic (PrSTL). SENTIL combines an efficient Rust core with universal ecosystem integration, delivering performance exceeding existing deterministic monitors while providing rigorous probabilistic guarantees through statistical model checking, sequential probability ratio testing, and adaptive rare event estimation. SENTIL employs streaming algorithms for incremental robustness computation, parallel Monte Carlo sampling, and a language-agnostic C-ABI enabling seamless deployment across ROS, Apollo, MATLAB Simulink, and AUTOSAR platforms, and direct integration in C, C++, Python, and Java. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed tool, we validate SENTIL across various scenarios spanning autonomous vehicle monitoring, medical device validation, and biological networks, demonstrating 10-1,000[MATH] performance improvements over existing tools while maintaining provable confidence intervals. SENTIL is open source ({}) and it positions probabilistic runtime verification as a deployable infrastructure for all real-world safety-critical stochastic systems.
tldr: SENTIL is a runtime verification tool for probabilistic temporal logic in stochastic cyber-physical systems, offering statistical guarantees and high performance.
motivation: Existing runtime verification tools lack support for probabilistic dynamics in stochastic CPS, despite theoretical foundations being established years ago.
method: The tool combines an efficient Rust core with statistical model checking, sequential probability ratio testing, adaptive rare event estimation, and streaming algorithms for incremental robustness computation.
result: SENTIL achieves 10-1000x performance improvements over existing tools while maintaining provable confidence intervals, validated across autonomous vehicle, medical device, and biological network scenarios.
conclusion: SENTIL positions probabilistic runtime verification as deployable infrastructure for safety-critical stochastic systems, with open-source availability enabling broad adoption.

title: Graph Structure Of Chebyshev Permutation Polynomials Over Binary And Ternary Adic Rings
authors: Xiaoxiong Lu, Yuling Dai, Chengqing Li
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the functional graph of a nonlinear map over a finite domain is crucial for analyzing its dynamical complexity and potential applications in cryptography and pseudorandom generation. In this paper, we investigate the graph structure of Chebyshev permutation polynomials over the ring [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are positive integers and [MATH]. Each element of the ring is regarded as a vertex, and the mapping relation defined by the polynomial corresponds to a directed edge. Building on new properties of Chebyshev polynomials modulo powers of [MATH] and [MATH], we provide an explicit characterization of path lengths and cycle structures in the functional graph. We show that, despite the complexities introduced by the binary and ternary components, the graph exhibits strong regularities, including a constant number of cycles of a given length and predictable branching patterns as [MATH] and [MATH] increase. Our results extend previous studies over prime-power rings, offering insights into the emergence of complexity in digital nonlinear maps and supporting the security analysis of their cryptographic applications.
tldr: This paper analyzes the functional graph structure of Chebyshev permutation polynomials over binary and ternary adic rings, focusing on cycle lengths and branching patterns.
motivation: To understand the dynamical complexity of nonlinear maps over finite domains for cryptographic and pseudorandom generation applications.
method: The authors study Chebyshev polynomials modulo powers of 2 and 3, characterizing path lengths and cycle structures in the functional graph using new properties of these polynomials.
result: The graph exhibits strong regularities, including constant numbers of cycles of given lengths and predictable branching patterns as the ring size increases.
conclusion: The results extend previous studies over prime-power rings and provide insights into the complexity of digital nonlinear maps, supporting security analysis of cryptographic applications.

title: Safeguarding Text-to-Image Generative Models Against Unauthorized Knowledge Distillation
authors: Yilan Gao, Sida Huang, Hongyuan Zhang, Xuelong Li
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Closed-weight generative services are increasingly deployed through query-based APIs, where users can obtain generated outputs while model parameters remain inaccessible. However, such deployment does not prevent model stealing: an attacker can repeatedly query the service, collect large volumes of released synthetic images, and use them as training data for a private substitute model. This query-output-driven process enables unauthorized knowledge distillation and capability replication without direct access to the original weights. To mitigate this threat, a practical defense should preserve the visual fidelity of released images, provide explicit control over perturbation magnitude, and scale efficiently to large-volume output release. We present WaveGuard, a single-pass, generator-based protection framework that safeguards released synthetic images under a user-specified perturbation budget. WaveGuard employs a frequency-aware perturbation generator to inject structured, imperceptible perturbations that maintain perceptual utility for benign viewers while reducing the usefulness of protected images as training data for unauthorized student models. Extensive experiments under WikiArt-related synthetic-output distillation settings show that WaveGuard achieves a favorable efficacy--fidelity--efficiency trade-off, with explicit imperceptibility control and substantial gains in protection efficiency.
tldr: WaveGuard is a defense framework that injects imperceptible frequency-domain perturbations into synthetic images to prevent unauthorized knowledge distillation of text-to-image generative models.
motivation: Closed-weight generative models are vulnerable to model stealing via query-based APIs, where attackers collect synthetic outputs to train substitute models. Existing defenses lack explicit perturbation control and efficiency for large-scale output release.
method: WaveGuard uses a frequency-aware perturbation generator to add structured, imperceptible noise to released synthetic images under a user-specified perturbation budget, degrading their utility as training data for unauthorized student models.
result: Experiments on WikiArt-related synthetic-output distillation show that WaveGuard achieves a favorable trade-off between protection efficacy, visual fidelity, and computational efficiency, with explicit imperceptibility control.
conclusion: WaveGuard provides a practical defense against model stealing in text-to-image services, but its applicability to other generative domains and robustness against adaptive attacks remain open questions.

title: Adversarial Trust Poisoning In Vehicular Collaborative Perception
authors: Yutong Liu, Chenyi Wang, Ming F. Li, Qingzhao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collaborative perception (CP) enables connected and autonomous vehicles to share sensor data and jointly reason about their environment. To defend against adversaries that fabricate or manipulate shared data, existing systems employ cross-vehicle inconsistency detection and trust estimation, penalizing vehicles whose observations conflict with the majority. In this work, we show that these defenses themselves introduce a new attack surface. We present TrustFlip, a novel attack that weaponizes consistency-based defenses to poison the trust assigned to benign vehicles. Instead of injecting false data into the collaboration pipeline, it deploys physical adversarial objects that are genuine but induce inconsistent observations among benign vehicles. The resulting inconsistencies are misattributed by the defense to the targeted vehicle, causing its trust score to degrade and eventually leading to its downweighting or exclusion from collaboration. Consequently, the system loses reliable sensing contributors, degrading perception capability and potentially inducing safety-critical failures. We evaluate TrustFlip across multiple collaborative perception architectures and defense mechanisms. Our results show that state-of-the-art defenses can be significantly affected: the attack removes the targeted benign vehicle from collaboration in up to 87.7% of scenarios and drops Average Precision (AP) by up to 13%. As an initial mitigation, we introduce TrustReflect, a lightweight self-reflection mechanism that marks disputed regions as uncertain and excludes them from trust evaluation, reducing the attack success rate by 35-100%.
tldr: This paper presents a novel attack on collaborative perception systems for autonomous vehicles that exploits trust estimation defenses to degrade benign vehicles' trust scores.
motivation: Existing defenses against data fabrication in vehicular collaborative perception rely on consistency-based trust estimation, but these defenses themselves can be weaponized by adversaries.
method: The authors propose TrustFlip, which deploys physical adversarial objects that cause inconsistent observations among benign vehicles, leading the defense to penalize the targeted vehicle's trust score.
result: TrustFlip removes the targeted benign vehicle from collaboration in up to 87.7% of scenarios and drops Average Precision by up to 13% across multiple architectures and defenses.
conclusion: The attack reveals a new vulnerability in collaborative perception systems; a lightweight self-reflection mechanism (TrustReflect) is introduced as a mitigation, reducing attack success by 35-100%.

title: Decision-Aware Quadratic ReLU Replacement For HE-Friendly Inference
authors: Rui Li, Wenyuan Wu, Weijie Miao
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) supports only additions and multiplications, so FHE-only neural-network inference typically replaces ReLU with polynomials fitted over empirical activation intervals. Such interval fitting often requires higher-degree polynomials to control activation error, incurring homomorphic evaluation costs, while classification is determined by the final logit decision. We revisit ReLU replacement from a decision-aware perspective: given a trained single-hidden-layer ReLU MLP and a specified calibration set, can an HE-friendly low-degree polynomial replace ReLU without retraining while preserving calibration-set decisions? We focus on quadratic replacement, the lowest-degree choice that retains a genuine per-unit nonlinearity. For calibration sets positive-margin separable in the lifted space, we formulate quadratic replacement as a linear separation problem, yielding necessary and sufficient conditions for calibration-lossless replacement and a constructive algorithm for the coefficients. When the positive-margin condition fails -- typically due to a few misclassified calibration samples -- we extend the same geometric framework via reduced convex hulls and Lagrangian-dual soft-margin relaxations, which bound the influence of any single sample, converting the problem into smaller convex quadratic programs that yield approximately feasible coefficients with high empirical agreement on calibration-set decisions. In particular, at the maximal weight cap [MATH], the reduced-convex-hull relaxation reduces to the convex-hull separation of the strictly separable case; the relaxation thus continuously extends the exact theory. Under CKKS, the quadratic replacement matches plaintext top-1 accuracy on multiple benchmarks, running 3.7--4.1[MATH] faster than Remez-7 in the activation module and 1.18--1.68[MATH] faster end-to-end.
tldr: This paper proposes a decision-aware quadratic ReLU replacement for homomorphic encryption-friendly neural network inference, focusing on preserving classification decisions with low-degree polynomials.
motivation: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) only supports addition and multiplication, requiring ReLU activation to be replaced by polynomials. Existing polynomial approximations often use high-degree polynomials to control activation error, which increases computational cost. This work aims to find low-degree (quadratic) replacements that preserve classification decisions without retraining.
method: The authors formulate quadratic ReLU replacement as a linear separation problem in a lifted space, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for lossless replacement when calibration samples are positive-margin separable. For non-separable cases, they extend the framework using reduced convex hulls and Lagrangian-dual soft-margin relaxations, converting the problem into convex quadratic programs.
result: The quadratic replacement achieves plaintext top-1 accuracy on multiple benchmarks under CKKS, with 3.7–4.1× speedup in the activation module and 1.18–1.68× end-to-end speedup compared to Remez-7.
conclusion: The proposed decision-aware quadratic replacement enables efficient FHE-friendly inference with minimal accuracy loss, and the geometric framework provides a principled way to design low-degree polynomial activations.

title: Joint Communication And Computation Scheduling For MEC-enabled Aigc Services: A Game-Theoretic Stochastic Learning Approach
authors: Huaizhe Liu, Xinyi Zhuang, Jiaqi Wu, Yuan Luo, Bin Cao, Lin Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) powered by Generative Diffusion Models (GDMs) has emerged as a transformative paradigm for automated content creation. To satisfy the stringent latency requirements of AIGC services in many edge intelligence scenarios (e.g., smart cities), Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) provides critical computational support by deploying GDMs at edge servers (ES) close to end users. This paper investigates an MEC-enabled AIGC network comprising multiple ES, wireless access points (APs), and mobile users (UEs) with heterogeneous latency and accuracy demands. We formulate a Joint Communication Association and Computation Offloading (JCACO) game, where each UE strategically selects its serving AP, ES, and inference steps to minimize the overall service completion time while meeting accuracy constraints. The problem is challenging due to the network dynamics and the incomplete information. We prove that the JCACO game is a potential game under both complete and stochastic information settings, ensuring the existence of Nash Equilibrium (NE) in both cases. To derive the NE efficiently, we develop a distributed Multi-Agent Stochastic Learning (MASL) algorithm that provably converges to the NE with strict performance guarantees. Unlike conventional best-response schemes, MASL requires neither the knowledge of other players' strategies nor global network information, making it fully distributed and adaptive to dynamic environments. We further provide a strict theoretical convergence analysis for MASL by using Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs). Simulation results demonstrate that MASL significantly reduces service completion time compared with benchmark methods while satisfying accuracy constraints, confirming its effectiveness and practicality for real-world MEC-enabled AIGC networks.
tldr: This paper proposes a game-theoretic stochastic learning approach for joint communication and computation scheduling in MEC-enabled AIGC services, focusing on latency and accuracy trade-offs.
motivation: To address the stringent latency requirements of AIGC services in edge intelligence scenarios by optimizing joint communication and computation decisions.
method: Formulates a Joint Communication Association and Computation Offloading (JCACO) game, proves it is a potential game, and develops a distributed Multi-Agent Stochastic Learning (MASL) algorithm that converges to Nash Equilibrium.
result: MASL significantly reduces service completion time compared to benchmarks while satisfying accuracy constraints, with theoretical convergence guarantees via ODE analysis.
conclusion: The proposed approach is effective and practical for real-world MEC-enabled AIGC networks, with potential for further optimization in dynamic environments.

title: Characterizing The Fault Response Of The Intel Neural Compute Stick 2 Under Single-Pulse Electromagnetic Fault Injection
authors: \v{s}tefan Ku\v{c}er\'ak, Jakub Breier, Xiaolu Hou
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision processing units and other commercial neural-network inference accelerators are increasingly deployed in safety-relevant edge applications, but their fault response under transient hardware disturbances remains poorly characterized in the open literature. For the Intel Movidius Myriad X, packaged as the Intel Neural Compute Stick 2 (NCS2), only a single feasibility study has been published. We report a systematic single-pulse electromagnetic fault injection (EMFI) campaign on the NCS2 running three ImageNet-trained convolutional neural networks (ResNet-18, ResNet-50, VGG-11) on the OpenVINO runtime. Across 1,536 spot-test trials at characterized hotspots and approximately 16,000 parameter-search trials, single pulses produce four reproducible outcome classes: no measured accuracy change, minor silent data corruption, major persistent degradation that survives across subsequent inferences until model reload, and device hangs requiring USB power-cycling; these outcomes are respectively interpreted as no-effect, SDC with possible SET-like or small persistent-state mechanisms, SEU-like persistent corruption, and SEFI-like loss of functionality. Two findings are central. First, the major-degradation class can be induced at 18-31% of trials at characterized hotspots, with post-collapse top-1 accuracy below five percent and persistence across all subsequent inferences until explicit model reload - a regime that no inference-API-level mechanism detects. Second, this regime is also inducible by pulses delivered to an idle device with the model already loaded, demonstrating that load-time integrity checks alone are insufficient. We discuss mitigation strategies graded by class, focusing on mechanisms implementable at the application level without modification to the device firmware or the OpenVINO runtime.
tldr: This paper experimentally characterizes the fault response of the Intel Neural Compute Stick 2 under electromagnetic fault injection, identifying four outcome classes and highlighting persistent silent data corruption that evades runtime detection.
motivation: Commercial neural-network accelerators are increasingly used in safety-critical edge applications, but their robustness to transient hardware faults is poorly understood. Only one prior feasibility study existed for the NCS2.
method: Systematic single-pulse electromagnetic fault injection (EMFI) was performed on the NCS2 running three ImageNet-trained CNNs (ResNet-18, ResNet-50, VGG-11) on the OpenVINO runtime, with 1,536 spot-test trials and ~16,000 parameter-search trials.
result: Four outcome classes were observed: no effect, minor silent data corruption, major persistent degradation (18-31% of trials at hotspots, top-1 accuracy <5%, persisting until model reload), and device hangs. The major degradation regime is also inducible on an idle device with the model already loaded.
conclusion: The findings reveal a vulnerability where persistent silent data corruption can go undetected by inference-API-level mechanisms, and load-time integrity checks are insufficient. Mitigation strategies at the application level are discussed.

title: EnCAgg: Enhanced Clustering Aggregation For Robust Federated Learning Against Dynamic Model Poisoning
authors: Tianyun Zhang, Zhen Yang, Haozhao Wang, Ru Zhang, Yongfeng Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning faces increasing threats from model poisoning attacks, which harms its application to improve privacy. Existing defense methods typically rely on fixed thresholds or perform clustering with a fixed number of clusters to distinguish malicious gradients from benign ones. However, these methods are difficult to adapt to dynamic poisoning strategies of malicious clients, and often result in the loss of benign gradients due to the heterogeneity of clients' local datasets. To address these problems, we propose a novel robust aggregation method that leverages a small number of known benign clients as references, enabling accurate identification and filtering of malicious gradients while retaining as many benign gradients as possible, even when the number of malicious clients is unknown and variable. First, we introduce a density-based low-dimensional gradient clustering method, which projects gradients onto the two most divergent dimensions and applies density-based clustering to identify malicious gradients while retaining clustered benign gradients and potentially benign outliers. Second, we design an enhancing clustering low-dimensional gradient generator model, which learns to generate pseudo-gradients aligned with the boundary of the benign cluster. These pseudo-gradients act as bridges to connect sparse benign gradient outliers. Third, we introduce low-dimensional gradient re-clustering that clusters the generated pseudo-gradients together with real gradients to recover benign gradients misclassified as noise points, enabling more benign gradients to participate in aggregation. Extensive experiments on the MNIST, CIFAR-10, and MIND datasets demonstrate that our method exhibits superior fidelity and robustness under dynamic poisoning scenarios.
tldr: This paper proposes a robust aggregation method for federated learning to defend against dynamic model poisoning attacks using density-based clustering and pseudo-gradient generation.
motivation: Existing defenses against model poisoning in federated learning are brittle to dynamic attack strategies and often discard benign gradients due to data heterogeneity.
method: The method uses a density-based low-dimensional gradient clustering with a small set of known benign clients as references, an enhancing clustering generator to create pseudo-gradients bridging sparse benign outliers, and re-clustering to recover misclassified benign gradients.
result: Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and MIND datasets show superior fidelity and robustness under dynamic poisoning scenarios compared to existing methods.
conclusion: The approach effectively adapts to unknown and variable numbers of malicious clients while preserving benign gradients, improving federated learning security.

title: Fluid Ris (FRIS)-Assisted Index Modulation For 6g Wireless Communications
authors: Xusheng Zhu, Kai-Kit Wong, Sai Xu, Hao Xu, Wen Chen, Hyundong Shin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluid reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (FRIS) extend conventional reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) by adding spatial reconfigurability through switchable apertures, pattern-reconfigurable units, fluidic conductive materials, or movable surface elements. This article studies how FRIS can support index modulation (IM), where information bits select a surface configuration and the receiver detects the index from the induced receiver-side response. A key challenge is that many feasible FRIS layouts do not necessarily lead to many reliable spatial indices. After propagation, mutual coupling, hardware distortion, and receiver observation, different layouts may produce similar receiver-side responses and cause index-detection errors. To address this issue, we present a response-aware design view, in which FRIS spatial codebooks are selected according to response-domain separability rather than layout diversity alone. We also discuss actuation granularity as a practical design knob that balances spatial diversity, pilot overhead, coupling robustness, and hardware feasibility. The resulting workflow helps select compact, trainable, and controllable spatial-index codebooks from dense FRIS layouts, providing design guidance for future programmable wireless environments.
tldr: This paper proposes a response-aware design for fluid reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (FRIS) to support index modulation in 6G wireless communications.
motivation: To address the challenge that many feasible FRIS layouts do not yield reliable spatial indices due to propagation, mutual coupling, and hardware distortion.
method: The authors present a response-aware design view where FRIS spatial codebooks are selected based on response-domain separability rather than layout diversity alone, and discuss actuation granularity as a design knob.
result: The proposed workflow helps select compact, trainable, and controllable spatial-index codebooks from dense FRIS layouts.
conclusion: The work provides design guidance for future programmable wireless environments, but is not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Multi-Winner Voting Games In Tu And Ntu: When Is The Core Always Non-Empty?
authors: Christian Hatschka Jiehua Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-winner approval voting selects a size-[MATH] committee that aggregates voters' approval preferences over a set of alternatives. A central question is coalitional stability: No coalition should be able to pick a committee -- of size at most its proportional share -- under which every coalition member has strictly more approved alternatives. This notion, introduced by Aziz et al. (2017) as core-stable committees, is naturally interpreted as a core notion with non-transferable utility. We introduce multi-winner voting games, a cooperative-game framework that unifies prior work and supports a systematic study of two utility-transfer models across different voting rules. Players are voters. Each coalition has a proportional seat cap and may only propose admissible committees up to that size. Fixing a multi-winner rule, each admissible committee induces a utility vector for the members of the coalition. In the transferable utility (TU) model, a coalition may redistribute the total utility of an admissible committee among its members. In the non-transferable utility (NTU) model, a coalition may only use utility vectors that are realized directly by some admissible committee. The core consists of utility vectors feasible for the grand coalition that are not blocked by any coalition. A coalition is blocking if it can propose an admissible committee that makes all its members strictly better off, directly in NTU and after redistribution in TU. When instantiated with the standard PAV/approval utility, the NTU-core is equivalent to the core-stable committee concept studied in prior work. To our knowledge, the TU-core for multi-winner voting has not been previously studied. We analyze core existence and computation for four prominent rules: Approval Voting (AV), Satisfaction Approval Voting (SAV), Chamberlin--Courant (CC), Proportional Approval Voting (PAV).
tldr: This paper studies core stability in multi-winner voting games under transferable and non-transferable utility models, focusing on existence and computation of core-stable committees for several voting rules.
motivation: To unify and extend prior work on core-stable committees in multi-winner approval voting by introducing a cooperative game framework that allows systematic study of utility transfer models.
method: The authors define multi-winner voting games with TU and NTU utility models, analyze core existence for four voting rules (AV, SAV, CC, PAV), and provide computational complexity results.
result: Core non-emptiness depends on the voting rule and utility model; for some rules the core is always non-empty, while for others it may be empty or computationally hard to find.
conclusion: The framework provides a foundation for studying coalitional stability in voting, with implications for designing stable committees, but the paper is purely theoretical and not directly applicable to the user's research interests.

title: Measuring Security Without Fooling Ourselves: Why Benchmarking Agents Is Hard
authors: Sahar Abdelnabi, Chris Hicks, Konrad Rieck, Ahmad-Reza Sadeghi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The benchmarks used to evaluate AI agents in security-critical roles suffer from crucial weaknesses. Building on recent empirical evidence, we characterize three core challenges that undermine security evaluations: benchmark vulnerabilities, temporal staleness, and runtime uncertainty. We then outline practical directions toward building more robust and trustworthy evaluation frameworks.
tldr: This paper discusses challenges in benchmarking AI agents for security, not related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To highlight weaknesses in current security benchmarks for AI agents.
method: Characterization of three core challenges based on empirical evidence.
result: Identified benchmark vulnerabilities, temporal staleness, and runtime uncertainty.
conclusion: Proposes directions for more robust evaluation frameworks.

title: Phase-edge Imaging Using Q-plate Shifts For Faster And Simpler Microscopy
authors: Jigme Zangpo, Hirokazu Kobayashi, Ryo Yasuhara
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a simplified method for isolating the edges of a phase object from the edges of an amplitude object using a 4f system with an off-axis q-plate. Instead of the four off-axis shifts of the q-plate required in previous work, we need only two shifts (along +/- x) combined with linear polarizers at 45 degrees and 135 degrees. The number of measurements is reduced by half, potentially doubling the acquisition speed. We derive the theoretical basis, showing that the resulting intensity corresponds to the phase gradient squared, with amplitude-object contributions eliminated. Experiments on two phase-amplitude object samples demonstrate amplitude-edge reduction up to 97.6% and correlation coefficients up to 0.78 (sample 1) and 0.75 (sample 2). In overlapping regions, the phase edge is partially recovered; full recovery would require additional processing such as inverse filtering. This research is useful for biological imaging applications where fast and simple phase-edge isolation is desired.
tldr: This paper presents a simplified microscopy method using q-plate shifts for phase-edge imaging, reducing measurements by half.
motivation: To develop a faster and simpler method for isolating phase edges in microscopy, particularly for biological imaging.
method: A 4f system with an off-axis q-plate and two shifts along +/- x combined with linear polarizers at 45° and 135°.
result: Achieved up to 97.6% amplitude-edge reduction and correlation coefficients up to 0.78 for phase-edge detection.
conclusion: The method doubles acquisition speed but requires additional processing for full phase-edge recovery; useful for biological imaging.

title: A Residual-Subspace Constraint Framework For Fourier Ptychographic Microscopy
authors: Sui-Peng Wang, Si-Yi Xie, Chang-Tao Cai, Zhun Wei, Rui Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reconstruction fidelity of computational optical imaging is fundamentally constrained by the model-reality gap, i.e., the inevitable discrepancy between idealized forward models and the physical imaging process. Conventional paradigms attempt to bridge this gap through exhaustive system calibration or explicit parameter estimation, which are often computationally intensive and prone to severe non-convex stagnation. This paper introduces a Residual-Subspace Constraint Framework (RSCF) to achieve robust Fourier ptychographic microscopy. Instead of treating residuals as unstructured errors, RSCF leverages subspace decomposition to decouple low-rank, systematic mismatches from stochastic noise, thereby isolating stable information manifolds that remain invariant to forward-model inaccuracies. By embedding this subspace constraint into the iterative engine, the framework selectively suppresses error-amplifying components, enabling high-fidelity phase and amplitude recovery without explicit hardware calibration. Numerical simulations and experimental validations demonstrate that RSCF yields superior convergence acceleration and artifact suppression under severe optical aberrations and LED misalignment. This information-centric paradigm provides a versatile, model-agnostic strategy to enhance robustness across diverse computational imaging modalities.
tldr: This paper introduces a Residual-Subspace Constraint Framework to improve reconstruction fidelity in Fourier ptychographic microscopy by decoupling systematic errors from noise.
motivation: To address the model-reality gap in computational optical imaging, where idealized forward models fail to capture physical imperfections, leading to poor reconstruction fidelity.
method: The framework uses subspace decomposition to separate low-rank systematic mismatches from stochastic noise, embedding this constraint into an iterative reconstruction engine to suppress error-amplifying components.
result: Numerical simulations and experiments show superior convergence acceleration and artifact suppression under severe optical aberrations and LED misalignment, without explicit hardware calibration.
conclusion: The information-centric paradigm offers a model-agnostic strategy to enhance robustness in computational imaging, with potential extensions to other modalities.

title: Bem For Variable Coefficient Second-order Problems
authors: Stefan A. Sauter Benedikt Gr\"a{\ss}le
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A novel boundary element method (BEM) removes the classical dependence on explicit fundamental solutions and extends quasi-optimal BEM discretisations to strongly elliptic operators with variable coefficients. The approach constructs a computable approximation of the boundary operator from a Galerkin discretisation of the underlying elliptic differential operator in a one-time preprocessing step, for instance by conforming finite elements. The resulting algebraic formulation retains the dimension reduction intrinsic to boundary integral methods and is compatible with standard data-sparse matrix compression techniques.
tldr: This paper presents a novel boundary element method for variable coefficient second-order problems that eliminates the need for explicit fundamental solutions.
motivation: Classical BEM requires explicit fundamental solutions, which are not available for variable coefficient operators. The authors aim to extend BEM to such problems.
method: They construct a computable approximation of the boundary operator via a Galerkin discretization of the underlying elliptic operator in a preprocessing step, using conforming finite elements.
result: The resulting algebraic formulation retains dimension reduction and is compatible with data-sparse matrix compression techniques.
conclusion: The method enables quasi-optimal BEM discretizations for strongly elliptic operators with variable coefficients, broadening the applicability of BEM.

title: Monotone Erasure Codes
authors: Vivien Bammert, Annalisa Cimatti, Orestis Alpos, Giuliano Losa, Christian Cachin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Erasure codes are a critical component in reliable storage systems today, and many blockchain systems use consensus protocols that involve erasure codes to reduce their communication cost. Existing erasure codes rely on a threshold failure assumption, but recent blockchain systems have departed from this simple model and use generalized failure assumptions. This paper introduces monotone erasure codes that respect arbitrary trust assumptions on a set of nodes. The paper first describes a method for constructing a monotone erasure code from any access structure given by a monotone Boolean formula. Next, the relevant notion of a linear monotone erasure code is introduced, which works on vectors over a finite field and where the encoding is a linear operation. We then focus on constructing linear monotone erasure codes: We give an efficient algorithm to construct linear monotone erasure codes for any access structure, and we show how to efficiently construct linear monotone erasure codes for the special case of partitioned access structures with minimal storage overhead. Last but not least, this work also shows how to use monotone erasure codes to obtain a communication-efficient, generalized version of the well-known asynchronous verifiable information dispersal (AVID) primitive, which is a key building block for developing efficient reliable broadcast and consensus protocols.
tldr: This paper introduces monotone erasure codes for arbitrary trust assumptions, focusing on blockchain and distributed storage, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Existing erasure codes rely on threshold failure assumptions, but modern blockchain systems use generalized trust structures, motivating the need for erasure codes that respect arbitrary access structures.
method: The authors define monotone erasure codes based on monotone Boolean formulas, introduce linear monotone erasure codes over finite fields, and provide efficient construction algorithms for general and partitioned access structures.
result: They present algorithms to construct linear monotone erasure codes for any access structure and achieve minimal storage overhead for partitioned structures, and demonstrate an application to asynchronous verifiable information dispersal.
conclusion: Monotone erasure codes enable communication-efficient consensus protocols under generalized failure assumptions, with potential impact on blockchain and distributed systems.

title: Autonomous Llm Agents & CTFs: A Second Look
authors: Youness Bouchari, Matteo Boffa, Marco Mellia, Idilio Drago, Thanh Minh Bui, Dario Rossi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly proposed to automate offensive security tasks, with recent studies reporting near human-level success rates in Capture-the-Flag (CTF) challenges. We here revisit these results, providing a second look at these claims. We engineer different agent architectures of increasing complexity and modularity on 30 web-based CTFs challenges spanning 14 vulnerability classes. We instantiate these agents with multiple LLM backbones, and compare them with claude-code, a general-purpose agent that automatically determines its internal architecture. Our evaluation yields three main findings. First, claude-code achieves performance comparable to the engineered architectures (19/30 solved tasks), suggesting that general-purpose agents are strong baselines for offensive security tasks. Second, both our architectures and claude-code struggle in the same challenge categories, revealing persistent barriers that keep current agents below human-level capability. Third, by leveraging our manually designed architectures we can systematically measure the impact of additional components, finding that structured orchestration of specialized roles outperforms monolithic designs, improving run-to-run consistency, and reducing execution costs.
tldr: This paper evaluates LLM agents on web-based CTF challenges, finding that general-purpose agents perform comparably to specialized architectures but still fall short of human-level capability.
motivation: To critically reassess claims that LLM agents achieve near human-level success in offensive security tasks, and to systematically compare different agent architectures.
method: Engineered multiple agent architectures of increasing complexity and modularity, tested on 30 web-based CTF challenges covering 14 vulnerability classes, using various LLM backbones and comparing with claude-code.
result: Claude-code solved 19/30 tasks, matching engineered architectures; both struggled in similar categories; structured orchestration of specialized roles improved consistency and reduced costs over monolithic designs.
conclusion: General-purpose agents are strong baselines for offensive security, but persistent barriers remain; future work should address these limitations to approach human-level performance.

title: HIDBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models For Host-Based Intrusion Detection
authors: Danyu Sun, Jinghuai Zhang, Yuan Tian, Zhou Li
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent benchmark efforts have advanced the evaluation of large language models (LLMs) in cybersecurity, including tasks such as penetration testing and vulnerability identification. However, a critical cybersecurity task, namely intrusion detection from system logs, remains unexplored. In this work, we present a new benchmark to assess LLMs' capabilities in supporting host-based intrusion detection systems (HIDS). This task requires fine-grained reasoning over large-scale, noisy, and highly imbalanced system logs, where complex interactions between benign and malicious activities make reliable detection challenging. Our benchmark unifies three public system log datasets, DARPA-E3, DARPA-E5, and NodLink, and introduces a data construction pipeline that transforms raw host telemetry into LLM-compatible inputs, enabling systematic evaluation under realistic intrusion detection settings. Our evaluation of frontier LLMs reveals substantial performance gaps across datasets. While many models achieve high precision (often above 0.8) on simpler datasets, their performance degrades significantly as system logs become noisier and more complex, with MCC frequently dropping below 0.5 and false positive rates increasing sharply. We further analyze model behavior and identify distinct regimes, including conservative detectors with low false positive rates and over-sensitive models that generate excessive alerts. Overall, our results highlight that while LLMs show strong potential for HIDS, their effectiveness is highly sensitive to data complexity, and robust system design is essential for reliable deployment.
tldr: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on host-based intrusion detection from system logs.
motivation: Intrusion detection from system logs is a critical cybersecurity task that has not been systematically benchmarked for LLMs.
method: The authors unify three public system log datasets and construct a pipeline to convert raw telemetry into LLM-compatible inputs, then evaluate frontier LLMs on detection performance.
result: LLMs achieve high precision on simpler datasets but performance degrades on noisier, more complex logs, with MCC often below 0.5 and high false positive rates.
conclusion: LLMs show potential for HIDS but their effectiveness is sensitive to data complexity, requiring robust system design for reliable deployment.

title: Polars Inside Intel Sgx2 Enclaves: An Empirical Study Of Confidential Analytical Query Processing
authors: Wei Wang, Burns Smith, Kenny Leftin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) have renewed interest in confidential analytics, but most prior evaluations focus on SQL database engines or earlier SGX generations. This paper studies an Arrow-native DataFrame engine, Polars, running inside Intel SGX2 enclaves via Gramine on TPC-H SF30 with Azure Blob Storage. We report both the standard TPC-H power score and a query-only variant that removes table-loading time in order to separate compute overhead from data-ingestion overhead. Across four dataset-width configurations (approximately 22-73 GB), end-to-end overhead remains nearly constant at 1.49-1.56[MATH], but this composite metric obscures two distinct behaviors: query-only overhead declines from 1.51-1.52[MATH] to 1.43-1.44[MATH], whereas table-loading overhead rises from 2.27[MATH] to 4.07[MATH]. We further show that overhead is not uniform across queries: for the len130 configuration, the median per-query SGX slowdown is 1.45[MATH] with a maximum of 2.57[MATH], and a small set of queries exhibits pronounced run-to-run spikes consistent with stateful EPC pressure. Finally, we compare Polars' lazy and eager APIs under the same TEE setting. Lazy execution is 2.25-2.27[MATH] faster overall, while eager execution fails with out-of-memory errors at 41 GB and above. Relative to the recent DuckDB-SGX2 study, our results suggest that SGX2 can support Arrow-native analytical processing with a similar order of security overhead, but that load-path amplification and API-level optimization are first-order determinants of end-to-end performance.
tldr: This paper evaluates the performance of the Polars DataFrame engine inside Intel SGX2 enclaves for confidential analytics, focusing on TPC-H benchmarks and comparing lazy vs eager APIs.
motivation: To understand the overhead of running Arrow-native analytical processing in trusted execution environments, as prior work focused on SQL engines or older SGX versions.
method: Empirical benchmarking of Polars inside SGX2 enclaves using Gramine on TPC-H SF30 with Azure Blob Storage, measuring end-to-end and query-only overhead across dataset widths.
result: End-to-end overhead is nearly constant (1.49-1.56x), but query-only overhead declines while table-loading overhead increases with dataset size; lazy execution is 2.25-2.27x faster than eager, which fails at 41 GB.
conclusion: SGX2 can support Arrow-native analytics with similar security overhead to SQL engines, but load-path amplification and API choice are critical for performance.

title: PEMark: Watermarking Api Responses Based On Proxy Gateways And Position Encoding
authors: Yifei Zhou, Xianjun Gu, Xinyu Dai, Ming Liu, Lansheng Han
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data leakage from API responses has drawn wide attention. APIs are often not fully regulated, making them easy to abuse. One common solution is to embed watermarks into API responses for traceability. However, existing watermarking methods often require modifying database content or API response data. This forces changes to business system code, and may even disrupt normal business operations because data values are altered. In this paper, we propose an original pluggable watermarking scheme based on a watermark proxy gateway and PEMark (Position Encoding-based Watermarking). The key novelty of our approach is exploiting the inherent permutation redundancy in the ordering of JSON/XML key-value pairs -- an overlooked dimension that carries no semantic information yet provides abundant encoding capacity. First, we forward server responses to the watermark proxy gateway, a design that requires zero modification to existing business systems. Then, we embed a watermark into each API response using position encoding, which reorders keys without altering any data values. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to achieve distortion-free API response watermarking via position encoding over a proxy gateway. Our method does not modify any data values, so normal business operations continue seamlessly after watermark embedding. Experimental results show that our framework maintains business usability while ensuring that returned API data is traceable. Compared with current mainstream schemes, our method is robust against tampering and insertion attacks (100\% similarity), and can withstand certain levels of deletion attacks.
tldr: This paper proposes a watermarking scheme for API responses that reorders JSON/XML key-value pairs to embed a watermark without altering data values.
motivation: Data leakage from API responses is a concern, and existing watermarking methods require modifying database content or response data, which can disrupt business operations.
method: The authors design a pluggable watermark proxy gateway that intercepts server responses and reorders key-value pairs using position encoding to embed a watermark, requiring zero changes to the business system.
result: The method achieves 100% similarity under tampering and insertion attacks and withstands certain deletion attacks, while maintaining business usability.
conclusion: The approach offers a distortion-free, robust watermarking solution for API responses, but its relevance to quantum computing or information thermodynamics is negligible.

title: Market-Analysis-Driven Methodology For Assessing Charging Station Cybersecurity
authors: Jakob L\"ow, Lukas Eder, Alexander M\"uller, Hans-Joachim Hof
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern charging communication standards for electric vehicles include optional security controls such as TLS-based authentication and encryption. However, with tens of thousands of fast charging points deployed in any given country, individually testing each one for security control support is infeasible. This paper proposes a scalable, extrapolation-based methodology for assessing charging station cybersecurity at a national level. A market analysis identifies operator-manufacturer pairs, enabling the targeted selection of charging stations for field testing, whose results can then be extrapolated to all stations sharing the same combination. We demonstrate this methodology for Germany, covering over 40000 CCS charging points as of December 2025. With a manageable number of field tests, our extrapolated data examines 51.9\% of german CCS charging stations. It shows that only 27.4\% of charging stations in our scope provide TLS-protected communication, despite widespread theoretical support.
tldr: This paper proposes a market-analysis-driven methodology to assess cybersecurity of electric vehicle charging stations at a national level, focusing on TLS support.
motivation: Individually testing tens of thousands of charging points for security controls is infeasible, so a scalable extrapolation method is needed.
method: A market analysis identifies operator-manufacturer pairs, then field tests a targeted subset and extrapolates results to all stations sharing the same combination.
result: Applied to Germany's 40,000+ CCS charging points, the method covers 51.9% of stations and finds only 27.4% provide TLS-protected communication.
conclusion: The methodology enables large-scale security assessment with limited field tests, highlighting a significant gap between theoretical support and actual deployment of TLS.

title: Landau-Ginzburg Models Of Generalised Dubrovin-Zhang Form And Pole Collision: Dynkin-type A
authors: Karoline van Gemst Alessandro Proserpio
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In arXiv:1711.05958, arXiv:2103.12673, the authors derive one-dimensional Landau-Ginzburg mirrors of Dubrovin-Zhang Frobenius manifolds constructed on regular orbit spaces of an extension of affine Weyl groups. We generalise the method employed, and classify the resulting Frobenius manifold structures in Dynkin type A. We interpret our results in terms of a stratification on the Hurwitz space boundary, and develop a pole-collision framework to compare the Frobenius structures within different strata. With this, we can prove a structural result at the level of the prepotential, for arbitrary rank and dimension, as a suitable renormalised limit of the formulae in arXiv:2412.05165. As a corollary, a conjecture of Ma and Zuo regarding the form of prepotentials related to doubly-extended affine Weyl groups is proven.
tldr: This paper develops Landau-Ginzburg models for generalized Dubrovin-Zhang Frobenius manifolds in Dynkin type A, focusing on pole collision and stratification of Hurwitz space.
motivation: To generalize previous work on one-dimensional Landau-Ginzburg mirrors and classify Frobenius manifold structures in Dynkin type A.
method: Generalization of methods from arXiv:1711.05958 and arXiv:2103.12673, using pole-collision framework and stratification on Hurwitz space boundary.
result: Classification of Frobenius manifold structures and proof of a conjecture by Ma and Zuo regarding prepotentials related to doubly-extended affine Weyl groups.
conclusion: The results provide structural insights into Frobenius manifolds and their prepotentials, with implications for singularity theory and integrable systems.

title: Lie Symmetries Of A Generalized Fisher Equation In Cylindrical Coordinates
authors: Uuganbayar Zunderiya Bayarjargal Batsukh
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we studied a generalized Fisher equation in cylindrical coordinate using Lie symmetry method. We have determined for what type of source function the generalized Fisher equation has Lie Symmetries other than time translation symmetry when the diffusion function is given by an exponential function. Also the reduced ordinary differential equations are obtained corresponding to Lie symmetries of the generalized Fisher equation.
tldr: This paper applies Lie symmetry analysis to a generalized Fisher equation in cylindrical coordinates, focusing on source functions that yield symmetries beyond time translation.
motivation: To extend the study of Fisher equations, which model population dynamics and reaction-diffusion systems, by incorporating cylindrical geometry and exponential diffusion, and to identify hidden symmetries.
method: Lie symmetry method is used to determine the infinitesimal generators of the generalized Fisher equation, and symmetry reductions are performed to obtain ordinary differential equations.
result: The conditions on the source function for which the equation admits additional Lie symmetries are derived, and reduced ODEs are presented.
conclusion: The work contributes to the classification of symmetries for nonlinear reaction-diffusion equations, but its direct relevance to quantum information or condensed matter physics is minimal.

title: A Path-finding Algorithm For Computing Minimal-weight-matching Centrosymmetry Parameter
authors: Vasily V. Pisarev
abstract: ArXiv:2605.22094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2020, Peter Larsen reported flaws in the methods for centrosymmetry parameter computation in the existing molecular dynamics and analysis packages. He proposed an intuitive an mathematically rigorous formulation for centrosymmetry parameter in terms of minimal-weight matching (MWM) on a fully-connected graph of atomic neighbors. He proposed using Edmonds' blossom algorithm for computing such a matching. In this paper, we investigate an alternative algorithm for MWM CSP computation using path finding approach and A* algorithm.
tldr: This paper proposes a path-finding algorithm using A* to compute the minimal-weight-matching centrosymmetry parameter, an alternative to Edmonds' blossom algorithm.
motivation: Existing methods for centrosymmetry parameter computation in molecular dynamics were found flawed; a rigorous formulation using minimal-weight matching was proposed but computationally expensive.
method: The authors investigate an alternative algorithm based on path finding and the A* algorithm to compute the minimal-weight matching for centrosymmetry parameter.
result: The paper presents a path-finding approach as an alternative to Edmonds' blossom algorithm for computing the minimal-weight-matching centrosymmetry parameter.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm may offer computational advantages, but the paper's abstract does not provide specific performance comparisons or results.

title: Another Perspective On Chatterjea Contraction
authors: Shallu Sharma, Irfan Ahmed, Sahil Billawria
abstract: ArXiv:2605.21549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by the well-known result stating that if any iterate of a mapping is a Banach contraction on a complete metric space, then the mapping itself possesses a unique fixed point, we investigate that claim for a Chatterjea contraction but by retaining the left-hand side of the inequality as per the mapping itself. With an additional assumption of k- continuity, the existence and uniqueness of a fixed point is obtained for a new class of contractions, m-Chatterjea contraction, on a complete metric space. Several examples are given in order to substantiate many theoretical claims such as discontinuity at the unique limit point of the iterative sequence, as well as examples demonstrating that this new class strictly contains the class of Chatterjea mappings.
tldr: This paper extends the concept of Chatterjea contractions to m-Chatterjea contractions and proves fixed point theorems under k-continuity.
motivation: To investigate whether the property that a mapping has a unique fixed point if some iterate is a Banach contraction holds for Chatterjea contractions, and to introduce a new class of contractions.
method: The authors define m-Chatterjea contractions and use k-continuity to prove existence and uniqueness of fixed points in complete metric spaces, with examples illustrating discontinuity.
result: A new class of contractions (m-Chatterjea) is introduced, and fixed point theorems are established; examples show this class strictly contains Chatterjea mappings and can be discontinuous at the fixed point.
conclusion: The work contributes to fixed point theory but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or the user's research interests.
